title: Civic Science Fellow, Evidence & Creator Partnerships 2026: $85,000 Fellowship at AcademyHealth.
summary: Are you an experienced communications, journalism, health policy, science communication, community engagement, or digital audience development professional interested in using evidence to reach wider public audiences? AcademyHealth is seeking a Civic Science Fellow, Evidence Creator Partnerships to lead an innovative 18-month initiative focused on connecting health policy research and evidence with social media creators, community communicators, and other trusted messengers. The fellowship, hosted by AcademyHealth , will focus on understanding how evidence can reach new and diverse audiences through creator partnerships, social media platforms, community networks, and civic dialogue. The successful candidate will lead an initiative titled “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy.” The project will seek to develop an Evidence Creator Pipeline connecting health policy research with social media creators and community communicators who influence civic conversations and reach millions of people. The fellowship is scheduled to run from September 2026 through March 2028 and offers a stipend of $85,000 per year . The position also includes paid leave, although health insurance and other benefits are not provided as part of the fellowship position. About the AcademyHealth Civic Science Fellowship AcademyHealth describes itself as the professional home and leading national organisation for health services researchers, policymakers, healthcare practitioners, and other stakeholders. Its work focuses on improving understanding of methods and data used in health services research, strengthening professional skills, supporting the use of evidence in policy and practice, and advocating for evidence-based improvements in health and healthcare. The organisation says it has also become a leading nonpartisan national voice on scientific integrity, federal data access, and the role of evidence in public debate. It emphasises an inclusive and equitable working environment and seeks to transform the field toward higher-impact and more equitable research. The Civic Science Fellow will become part of this environment while leading a major project at the intersection of: Health policy Evidence and research Science communication Social media Creator partnerships Community engagement Audience development Civic dialogue Digital communications Public-interest communication What Is the Evidence Creator Partnerships Fellowship? The Civic Science Fellow will lead an 18-month initiative designed to explore how evidence-based health policy information can reach audiences beyond traditional academic, scientific, and health policy institutions. The initiative recognises that social media creators, community communicators, journalists, and other trusted messengers can play an important role in shaping how people encounter and interpret information. Rather than relying solely on traditional methods of communicating research, the project will investigate how organisations can develop relationships with creators and community communicators who already have established audiences and trusted relationships. The Fellow will therefore combine: Landscape research Relationship building Audience and network analysis Creator recruitment Partnership development Content experimentation Communications strategy Knowledge sharing Toolkit development Sustainability planning The ultimate goal is to understand who can effectively carry evidence into new audiences, what makes creator partnerships successful, and how organisations can build sustainable networks of trusted evidence creators. About the “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy” Initiative The central project is titled “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy.” The initiative will build an Evidence Creator Pipeline that connects health policy research with social media creators, community communicators, and other trusted messengers. The project will pay particular attention to audiences that may not traditionally engage with scientific, academic, or health policy organisations. This includes an interest in: Cross-partisan audiences Nontraditional audiences Diverse communities Social media audiences Community networks Trusted messengers Alternative routes through which evidence can reach the public The Fellow will not simply conduct research and produce a report. They will also apply the findings through live AcademyHealth communications and engagement initiatives. This means the position combines research with practical experimentation. The Fellow will use AcademyHealth s organisational priorities as opportunities to test different approaches, learn from the results, and refine the Evidence Creator model. Key Responsibilities of the Civic Science Fellow The successful Fellow will have significant responsibility for designing and implementing the project. 1. Conduct a Landscape Assessment The Fellow will lead a landscape assessment of social media creators and community communicators working at the intersection of: Health Policy Evidence The assessment will include a survey and rapid network analysis. The purpose will be to understand factors such as: What drives trust among audiences How different audiences interact with information Audience dynamics Preferred partnership models The characteristics of potential evidence creators How evidence moves through different networks 2. Identify and Recruit Evidence Creators The Fellow will develop and execute a strategy for identifying and recruiting a cohort of 5 to 10 emerging evidence creators . The cohort is expected to represent diverse: Backgrounds Platforms Communities Audiences Experiences The goal is to identify creators who can potentially help communicate evidence to audiences that may not normally engage with traditional health policy or scientific institutions. 3. Develop Creator Partnership Models The Fellow will pilot different partnership approaches with the selected creators. These partnerships may involve: Compensation Skill-building Content co-creation A combination of these approaches Importantly, the partnership models will be co-designed with the creators themselves . This means the Fellow will need strong relationship-building skills and the ability to understand the needs, interests, audiences, and working styles of potential partners. 4. Develop and Produce Pilot Content The Fellow will oversee the development and production of pilot content pieces. The content will be: Co-created with members of the creator cohort. Designed for public audiences. Distributed across at least three platforms. This responsibility makes the position particularly relevant to professionals with experience in social media, digital communications, content strategy, creator partnerships, audience development, or public-interest communications. 5. Develop a Publicly Available Toolkit Another major responsibility will be creating protocols and a publicly available toolkit. The toolkit will be designed so that other scientific societies can use it to develop similar evidence creator networks. This means the Fellow will need to document what works, develop practical processes, and translate lessons from the project into resources that other organisations can apply. 6. Present Findings The Fellow will present project findings at the AcademyHealth Annual Research Meeting . They will also contribute to a final report intended for broad dissemination. The ability to communicate findings clearly to professional and public audiences will therefore be important. 7. Develop a Sustainability Plan The Fellow will develop a plan for sustaining the Evidence Creator Network beyond the fellowship period. This responsibility involves thinking beyond the initial 18-month project and considering how the network, partnerships, and lessons developed during the fellowship can continue to have an impact. 8. Establish and Manage an Advisory Group The Fellow will also establish and manage a project advisory group. The advisory group will draw on: AcademyHealth staff AcademyHealth members External experts Professionals with expertise in network analysis Experts in policy influence Health communications specialists The Fellow will therefore need to be comfortable coordinating multiple stakeholders and managing relationships across different professional areas. Who Is AcademyHealth Looking For? AcademyHealth is looking for an emerging leader who is comfortable working with complex and ambiguous challenges. The ideal candidate should be able to take an idea from the concept stage through to implementation. The organisation is seeking someone who can: Work independently. Build relationships with people from different backgrounds and areas of expertise. Translate complex evidence into compelling ideas. Communicate effectively with public audiences. Understand how people encounter and interpret information. Explore new approaches to connecting evidence with civic dialogue. Develop innovative approaches to creator and community partnerships. Manage a major project with multiple stakeholders. Adapt as the initiative develops. AcademyHealth also states that applicants do not need to meet every listed expectation in order to apply. The organisation welcomes applications from a broad range of candidates and values diverse perspectives, backgrounds, experiences, and skills. Desired Qualifications Applicants should carefully consider the qualifications outlined by AcademyHealth before applying. Educational Qualification A Bachelor s degree from an accredited college or university is required . A Master s degree is preferred , although it is not listed as mandatory. Professional Experience Candidates should have approximately 3 to 5 years of substantive professional experience in one or more relevant fields. These include: Health communications Science communications Health policy Journalism Community engagement Related fields The position is therefore aimed at candidates with meaningful professional experience rather than applicants who are completely new to communications or public engagement. Project Management Experience Applicants should have demonstrated experience managing or leading a complex project involving multiple stakeholders and moving parts. This is particularly important because the Fellow will be responsible for an 18-month initiative involving creators, researchers, policymakers, community organisations, AcademyHealth staff, members, and external experts. Creator, Influencer or Partnership Strategy Experience AcademyHealth is seeking candidates with experience developing or executing: Influencer strategies Creator strategies Audience-development strategies Partnership strategies Experience with public-interest, scientific, health, or policy organisations is particularly relevant. Social and Digital Platform Knowledge Candidates should understand social and digital platforms as ecosystems for: Audience development Relationship building Civic engagement Community engagement Content strategy Audience growth Creator partnerships This means the opportunity may be particularly attractive to professionals with backgrounds in digital communications, social media strategy, content creation, journalism, communications, or audience development. For more information, VISIT HERE. Relationship-Building Skills Applicants should be able to identify potential partners and establish credible, authentic, and productive relationships across different sectors and communities. These relationships may involve: Researchers Policymakers Community organisations Content creators Professional networks External experts Strong interpersonal and networking skills will therefore be essential. Ability to Experiment and Adapt The successful candidate should have experience experimenting with new communication or engagement approaches. AcademyHealth is particularly interested in candidates who can use: Audience insights Partner feedback Evidence Project results to refine and improve strategies. Communication Skills Highly developed written and oral communication skills are required. The Fellow must be able to take complex or technical subject matter and transform it into: Compelling narratives Public-facing content Engagement strategies Accessible communications This is an important component of the role because the project is specifically concerned with helping evidence reach non-specialist audiences. Understanding Communities and Trust Applicants should demonstrate curiosity about how different communities: Form opinions Establish trust Encounter information Engage with information Respond to evidence The ability to understand differences between communities and audiences will be important to the project s focus on diverse and nontraditional audiences. APPLY HERE. Health Policy Knowledge Knowledge of health policy issues is preferred . It is therefore an advantage for candidates who have previous exposure to health policy, health services research, healthcare communications, or related subjects. Self-Motivation and Project Management The Fellow should be self-motivated and have strong project management abilities. They will be expected to manage an evolving 18-month initiative with limited supervision. This makes independence, organisation, prioritisation, adaptability, and initiative important qualities for the position. Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to valuing diversity and contributing to inclusive working and learning environments. AcademyHealth emphasises the importance of diversity within its organisational culture. AcademyHealth Allows Flexibility in Candidate Backgrounds One important aspect of the opportunity is that AcademyHealth says it remains flexible regarding the types and depth of training and experience that potential Fellows may bring. The organisation indicates that it expects to work with the selected Fellow to refine the project scope according to the Fellow s background and help ensure the project s success. This means candidates should not necessarily eliminate themselves from consideration simply because their professional experience does not match every single item in the desired qualifications list. Fellowship Duration The Civic Science Fellowship is an 18-month fellowship position . The scheduled fellowship period is: September 2026 – March 2028 This is a substantial professional fellowship rather than a short-term internship or brief mentorship programme. The Fellow will be responsible for leading a major initiative while also participating in the broader Civic Science Fellows cohort. Fellowship Time Commitment The Fellow will spend approximately: 75% of their time , equivalent to approximately 30 hours per week , working with AcademyHealth as the host organisation. 25% of their time , approximately 10 hours per week , participating in shared learning and networking activities as part of the Fellows cohort. The cohort activities include weekly virtual sessions and an in-person convening. This structure means the fellowship combines direct project work with professional development, peer learning, and networking. Weekly Fellows Labs From September 2026 through September 2027 , the Fellow will participate in weekly virtual Fellows Labs. These sessions take place on: Tuesdays, 12:00 p.m. to 2:00 p.m. Eastern Time The sessions are designed to support: Shared learning Peer exchange Professional development Collaboration across the Fellows cohort This component provides Fellows with opportunities to learn alongside other professionals participating in the Civic Science Fellows programme. Fellowship Stipend The Civic Science Fellows programme provides a stipend of: $85,000 per year The position also includes paid leave . However, applicants should note that health insurance and other benefits are not provided as part of this fellowship position. The stipend is described as being set by the Civic Science Fellows programme. Work Location and Remote Work AcademyHealth operates a hybrid work environment , with options for remote and office work. Importantly, candidates do not need to be physically located in the Washington, DC area. The organisation specifically encourages candidates who live outside the Washington, DC area to apply. This makes the opportunity potentially accessible to professionals who are not based in Washington, DC. However, applicants should carefully consider the programme s required travel commitments before applying. Travel Requirements Some travel is required as part of the fellowship. The source identifies required participation in: The Civic Science Fellows and Partners Convening in February 2027 . The AcademyHealth Annual Research Meeting in Boston in 2027 . Travel costs associated with required fellowship activities are covered by the fellowship grant. Applicants should therefore be prepared to participate in required in-person fellowship activities when necessary. Equal Opportunity and Diversity AcademyHealth states that it is an Equal Opportunity Employer . The organisation says applicants and employees will receive equal opportunity regardless of factors including: Sex Race Colour Religion National origin Age Marital status Personal appearance Sexual orientation Family responsibilities Disability Matriculation Political affiliation Source of income Place of business or residence The organisation also states that diversity is an integral part of its organisational culture and that it seeks to maintain staff diversity at all levels. Who Can Apply? The opportunity is intended for qualified professionals whose background aligns with the fellowship s focus on evidence, health communications, science communications, public engagement, social media, creator partnerships, audience development, journalism, or related fields. The source does not specify a particular nationality, race, country, or continent as an eligibility requirement. Instead, AcademyHealth describes itself as an Equal Opportunity Employer and says it welcomes a broad range of candidates. Candidates should therefore focus on demonstrating the required education, professional experience, communication abilities, project management skills, partnership experience, and interest in evidence-based civic engagement. Is This a Fellowship? Yes. This opportunity is explicitly described by AcademyHealth as an 18-month fellowship position . The fellowship runs from September 2026 to March 2028 , provides an annual stipend of $85,000 , includes paid leave, and combines project work with shared learning and networking activities. It should therefore be categorised as a Fellowship , rather than a job, internship, scholarship, grant, competition, conference, or award. Application Requirements Qualified applicants are asked to submit: A resume A cover letter Applications should be submitted to AcademyHealth Human Resources by email at: jobs@academyhealth.org The organisation states that its hiring process will be conducted virtually, with interviews taking place by phone or video. Applicants can also visit the AcademyHealth website for additional information. Is There an Application Deadline? The provided opportunity announcement does not state a specific application deadline . Therefore, prospective applicants should not assume a deadline that is not included in the announcement. Because the fellowship is scheduled to begin in September 2026 , interested candidates should review the official AcademyHealth opportunity information and contact the organisation if they require confirmation of the current application status or closing date. Why This Fellowship Could Be Valuable The Civic Science Fellow position offers an opportunity to work at the intersection of several rapidly evolving areas. These include: Science communication Health policy Digital media Social media Creator partnerships Public engagement Community communications Audience development Evidence-based communication Civic dialogue Network building The Fellow will not only conduct research but will also develop practical partnerships, test communication models, produce content, create a publicly available toolkit, present findings, and develop a sustainability strategy. This makes the fellowship particularly relevant for professionals interested in developing innovative approaches to communicating evidence to wider audiences. Professional Development and Networking Another significant component of the fellowship is participation in the wider Civic Science Fellows network. The programme brings together professionals including: Scientists Scholars Community leaders Journalists Educators Media producers Public-interest organisations Funders The broader Civic Science Fellows programme is designed to encourage collaboration between science, diverse communities, and civil society. Fellows and host organisations work on new pilots, partnerships, knowledge, models, and approaches to civic science. The programme therefore provides not only an opportunity to lead an individual project but also to become part of a wider network of people working to strengthen connections between science, technology, innovation, communities, and civil society. For example, a candidate may have experience in: Health communications Science communications Journalism Digital communications Social media Community engagement Public policy communications Audience development Creator partnerships Influencer partnerships Content strategy Public-interest communications However, applicants should not assume that they need to come from one specific professional background. AcademyHealth states that it remains flexible regarding the types and depth of training and experience candidates may bring. Final Thoughts The Civic Science Fellow, Evidence Creator Partnerships opportunity at AcademyHealth is an 18-month professional fellowship focused on an increasingly important challenge: finding effective ways to connect research and evidence with wider public audiences. Through the “Bridging Science and Social Media for Better Health Policy” initiative, the successful Fellow will research creator and community networks, recruit 5–10 emerging evidence creators, develop partnership models, oversee content creation across multiple platforms, build a publicly available toolkit, present findings, and develop a sustainability plan for the Evidence Creator Network. The fellowship offers a $85,000 annual stipend , paid leave, remote and hybrid working options, professional development through the Civic Science Fellows cohort, and opportunities to participate in significant research and communications activities. title: ACET Procurement Intern 2026 in Ghana: Apply for Procurement and Supply Chain Opportunity in Accra.
summary: The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is inviting qualified candidates to apply for its Procurement Intern position in Accra, Ghana. The opportunity provides professional exposure to procurement operations within a Pan-African economic policy organisation and involves supporting procurement activities across institutional and donor-funded projects. The position is based in Accra and is expected to run from the time of appointment through 31 December 2026 . ACET is seeking a candidate with a relevant Bachelor s degree and practical procurement experience who can support purchasing, tendering, supplier management, contract administration, procurement planning, compliance, record keeping, and stakeholder coordination. ACET Procurement Intern Opportunity 2026 The African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) is a Pan-African economic policy institute focused on supporting Africa s long-term economic growth through transformation. The organisation works directly with African governments, businesses, and civil society across countries and borders to help remove policy barriers to sustainable and inclusive development. ACET is headquartered in Accra, Ghana , while maintaining a diverse workforce across several continents. The organisation describes itself as African-led and globally connected, drawing on the expertise of its staff and partners to conduct research, provide policy advice, and amplify Africa s voice through events, advocacy, and engagement. The Procurement Intern will join ACET s procurement function and work under the supervision of the Procurement Specialist . Position Details Details Information Organisation African Center for Economic Transformation (ACET) Position Procurement Intern Location Accra, Ghana Reporting to Procurement Specialist Duration Immediate through 31 December 2026 Posted 1 September 2026 Application deadline 11 September 2026 Application documents CV and Cover Letter The position is specifically designed to support ACET s procurement function across institutional and donor-funded activities. What Does the ACET Procurement Intern Do? The Procurement Intern will support the day-to-day delivery of procurement activities. Working under the Procurement Specialist, the successful candidate will coordinate assigned procurement processes, maintain procurement records and systems, support tendering and evaluation, assist with contract administration, and ensure procurement activities comply with ACET policies, applicable donor requirements, and established procedures. The role requires strong organisation, attention to detail, integrity, responsiveness, and the ability to complete assigned procurement responsibilities within established procedures and delegated authority. Procurement Operations and Support Responsibilities A major part of the role will involve supporting routine procurement operations. The Procurement Intern will be responsible for activities such as: Receiving and processing procurement requests. Confirming that required documentation is complete before procurement begins. Preparing purchase orders and work orders for goods and non-consulting services. Processing documents through the required approval channels. Coordinating supplier and bidder invitations. Receiving and maintaining the safe custody of bids and proposals. Maintaining procurement records. Supporting the identification and sourcing of qualified suppliers and service providers. Working with user departments to ensure procurement requirements and specifications are properly addressed. Preparing solicitation and tender documents using approved ACET templates. Monitoring procurement timelines. Following up with suppliers, user departments, and other stakeholders regarding outstanding actions. Providing internal requesters with timely updates about the progress of procurement activities. These responsibilities mean that the successful candidate will need to be highly organised and comfortable working with documents, suppliers, internal departments, deadlines, and established procurement procedures. Tendering, Evaluation and Award Support The Procurement Intern will also support ACET s tendering and evaluation processes. Responsibilities include: Coordinating pre-bid or pre-proposal meetings where applicable. Supporting clarification processes. Assisting with bid or proposal opening sessions where applicable. Providing administrative and procedural support to evaluation panels. Preparing evaluation materials. Preparing minutes and other records required during evaluations. Checking evaluation documentation for completeness and consistency. Submitting relevant documentation to the Procurement Specialist for review. Preparing draft award and notification documents. Preparing notifications for successful and unsuccessful bidders as directed. This part of the role provides exposure to the procurement cycle beyond purchasing, including tender preparation, evaluation administration, award documentation, and communication with bidders. Contract Administration Responsibilities Contract administration is another important component of the position. The Procurement Intern will assist with: Preparing draft contracts. Preparing purchase orders and agreements. Using approved templates for procurement documentation. Maintaining and updating the contract register. Recording contract values. Tracking key contract dates. Monitoring deliverables and milestones. Recording renewal dates. Monitoring assigned contracts. Following up on supplier and consultant deliverables. Following up on routine performance issues. Preparing draft contract extensions, amendments, and variations for review. Supporting contract close-out. Ensuring that required documentation, deliverables, and acceptance records are completed. This means candidates interested in developing experience in procurement and contract management could gain exposure to several stages of the contract lifecycle. Procurement Planning, Monitoring and Reporting The successful candidate will also support procurement planning and reporting activities. This includes: Supporting the Procurement Specialist in preparing and updating annual procurement plans. Supporting project procurement plans. Maintaining procurement trackers. Monitoring assigned procurement activities. Identifying procurement delays and outstanding actions. Reporting delays promptly to the Procurement Specialist. Assisting with procurement activity reports. Supporting donor procurement reports. Compiling documentation required for audits. Organising records required for reviews and management reporting. These duties require candidates to have strong record-keeping and organisational skills and the ability to monitor several activities at the same time. Compliance, Integrity and Procurement Records Procurement requires strict adherence to procedures, transparency, and accountability. The Procurement Intern will therefore support compliance by: Ensuring assigned procurement activities follow ACET procedures. Ensuring applicable donor requirements are followed. Maintaining complete and auditable procurement files. Supporting screening of bidders, suppliers, and consultants against applicable sanctions and debarment lists before awards. Administering conflict-of-interest declarations for evaluation panel members. Maintaining relevant conflict-of-interest records. Maintaining supplier files and contract documentation. Following ACET s record-retention requirements. Uploading and updating procurement documents on InSoft and applicable donor procurement or project-tracking systems. Promptly reporting suspected fraud, corruption, collusion, coercion, conflicts of interest, or other procurement irregularities to the Procurement Specialist. Integrity is therefore a particularly important aspect of the position. APPLY HERE. Stakeholder Support and Communication The Procurement Intern will interact with internal departments as well as external suppliers and service providers. The role includes: Providing professional procurement support to user departments. Supporting project teams. Assisting internal stakeholders. Providing procedural guidance under the direction of the Procurement Specialist. Reviewing draft Terms of Reference and specifications for completeness. Identifying gaps in procurement documentation. Communicating with bidders, suppliers, and consultants on routine procurement matters. Providing accurate information within authorised parameters. Supporting responses to procurement-related queries from internal and external stakeholders. Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills will therefore be useful for applicants. Other Procurement Duties In addition to the core responsibilities, the Procurement Intern may also: Support basic market research. Help identify potential suppliers. Contribute information that can assist with procurement activities and cost estimates. Improve procurement records and templates. Contribute to procurement trackers. Support improvements to administrative processes. Provide procurement support to other organisational units during periods of increased workload. Perform other procurement-related duties assigned by the Procurement Specialist. The position may therefore involve a combination of routine procurement administration, research, documentation, stakeholder communication, and process improvement. Candidates must meet one of the following three routes : Route 1: Bachelor s Degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management Applicants may qualify with: A Bachelor s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management; and At least two years of relevant procurement experience following the Bachelor s degree. Route 2: Bachelor s Degree in a Related Discipline Applicants may qualify with: A Bachelor s degree in a related discipline; and At least three years of relevant procurement experience following the Bachelor s degree. Route 3: Master s Degree Applicants may qualify with: A Master s degree in Procurement and Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or a related field; and At least one year of relevant procurement experience following the Master s degree. title: Become an Ambassador at the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly: Apply by September 18, 2026
summary: The 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program is an opportunity for young leaders who have previously participated in the AFS Youth Assembly to take on a representative and leadership role within the global AFS Youth Assembly community. The program is designed for young people who want to become pioneers in their communities, amplify youth voices on the global stage, promote youth participation in the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and represent the mission and programs of the AFS Youth Assembly. Ambassadors serve as official representatives of the AFS Youth Assembly for a one-year term. During this period, they are expected to promote Youth Assembly programs and initiatives, encourage other young people to participate, and nominate youth to become delegates. Applications are currently open, and interested candidates must complete the application process before the stated deadline. AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program 2027 The AFS Youth Assembly is a global platform focused on cultivating a network of young leaders and changemakers through exchange, education, action and impact. The Ambassador Program builds on this mission by giving previous Youth Assembly delegates an opportunity to remain engaged with the organization and contribute to its wider youth leadership network. According to the program, ambassadors are expected to become pioneers in their communities, help young people have a voice at the global level, and represent the mission of the AFS Youth Assembly. Successful ambassadors serve as official representatives of the Youth Assembly and take part in activities that promote its programs and initiatives. What Does an AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Do? An ambassador serves for a one-year term and has an active role in promoting the AFS Youth Assembly. The main responsibilities include: Representing the AFS Youth Assembly Ambassadors serve as official representatives and help communicate the organization s mission, programs and opportunities to young people in their communities and networks. Promoting Youth Assembly Programs Ambassadors are responsible for disseminating information about AFS Youth Assembly programs and initiatives. This may involve communicating opportunities through personal networks, schools, universities, youth organizations and digital platforms. Nominating Young People Ambassadors are expected to nominate youth who may be interested in becoming delegates at the AFS Youth Assembly. Conducting Engagement Activities Ambassadors may promote and represent the Youth Assembly through activities such as: Speaking at events Participating in radio programs Appearing on podcasts Participating in television shows Writing blogs Creating social media posts Conducting other engaging promotional activities These activities provide ambassadors with opportunities to communicate with different audiences and encourage greater youth participation in the Youth Assembly. Qualifications for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program The Ambassador Program has several specific eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review these requirements before submitting an application. Previous AFS Youth Assembly Participation Applicants must have attended the AFS Youth Assembly as a Delegate . This is an important requirement because the Ambassador Program is specifically geared toward youth who have previously participated in the Youth Assembly. Current Education or Organizational Affiliation Applicants must either: Be currently pursuing an undergraduate, graduate or postgraduate degree at a recognized academic institution during the present academic year; or Be affiliated with or represent an organization with a mission similar to that of the AFS Youth Assembly. This allows the program to consider both students and young people actively connected with relevant organizations. Active Role in School or Community Applicants should demonstrate that they have an active role within their school or community. This may include participation in youth initiatives, community activities, leadership programs, organizations or other forms of civic engagement. Knowledge and Experience With the Sustainable Development Goals Applicants should have experience and knowledge in working on the Sustainable Development Goals . The program is therefore particularly relevant to young people who have already engaged with global development, sustainability, community development or related initiatives. Commitment to Youth Empowerment Candidates should demonstrate a commitment to: Youth empowerment The Sustainable Development Goals Giving young people greater opportunities to participate Supporting youth voices and leadership Self-Starter and Problem Solver The program seeks candidates who are proactive and capable of identifying and addressing challenges independently. Being a self-starter is important because ambassadors are expected to actively promote the Youth Assembly and carry out activities during their one-year term. Social Media and Content Creation Skills Applicants should be social media savvy and have experience creating content. The program specifically identifies experience with formats such as: Short videos TikTok content Social media posts Other digital content These skills are relevant because ambassadors will play a role in communicating Youth Assembly opportunities and initiatives through different platforms. Communication and Coordination Skills Excellent communication and coordination skills are also required. Ambassadors may communicate with young people, organizations, event audiences, media platforms and the Youth Assembly team, making effective communication particularly important. Fundraising and Sponsorship Experience Experience in fundraising and sponsorship development is listed as a plus . This means it is beneficial but is not presented as a mandatory qualification. Candidates with experience developing partnerships, raising funds or securing sponsorships may therefore have an additional strength in their application. Responsibilities and Standards for AFS Ambassadors Being selected as an ambassador involves ongoing responsibilities throughout the one-year term. Ambassadors are expected to complete their assigned activities and maintain appropriate standards when representing the Youth Assembly. Reporting and Measuring Progress Ambassadors must complete an online report and present their strategy and progress using: Metrics Photos Specific activities conducted This means successful ambassadors should be prepared to document their activities and demonstrate what they have accomplished during their term. Completing Assignments Ambassadors are expected to complete assignments fully and before the applicable deadlines. Reliability and timely completion are therefore important elements of the ambassador role. Using the Official Promotional Materials Ambassadors must use the Youth Assembly s communication promo kit and follow the relevant protocols when presenting information about Youth Assembly programs. This helps ensure consistency and accuracy when ambassadors communicate publicly about the organization. Providing Accurate Information Ambassadors must always present accurate information about Youth Assembly programs. This is particularly important when promoting opportunities to potential delegates and other young people. Following the Code of Conduct Ambassadors are expected to follow the organization s code of conduct and uphold its stated values. These include: Professionalism Integrity Respect for Diversity Friendship Benefits of Becoming an AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador The Ambassador Program provides several potential benefits for selected participants. Certificate of Recognition Ambassadors can receive a Certificate of Recognition for their dedication and work with the AFS Youth Assembly. This provides formal recognition of their contribution during the ambassador term. Potential Speaking Opportunities Ambassadors may receive potential opportunities to speak at events. These experiences can help young leaders strengthen their public speaking and communication skills. Conference Fee Waivers Ambassadors may receive complimentary AFS Youth Assembly conference fee waivers , subject to applicable conditions. Delegate Discounts Ambassadors may also receive discounts for delegates attending the AFS Youth Assembly, subject to conditions. Professional Networking The program provides opportunities to build a professional network. Ambassadors can interact with other young leaders, Youth Assembly participants and individuals connected to the broader AFS network. Professional Development Ambassadors have opportunities to enhance their skills and professional development through their activities and engagement with the Youth Assembly. Opportunities to Attend AFS Youth Assemblies The program provides opportunities for ambassadors to attend AFS Youth Assemblies, subject to applicable conditions. Youth Leadership Experience Serving as an ambassador provides a leadership opportunity for young people who want to inspire and engage other youth around global challenges and the Sustainable Development Goals. Opportunity to Publish Online Ambassadors may have opportunities to publish content online as part of their engagement with the Youth Assembly. Outstanding Ambassador Recognition The program also provides additional recognition for ambassadors who perform their responsibilities with excellence. Outstanding Ambassadors will receive Outstanding Ambassador recognition . According to the program information, outstanding ambassadors will also receive special mention at the Youth Assembly and may be promoted through the Youth Assembly s social media platforms. Ambassador status and recognition are determined based on factors including: Quality of work Level of activity in promoting the Youth Assembly Effectiveness of promotional activities Completion of assigned tasks Communication with the Youth Assembly team Efforts to promote and support the Youth Assembly Quality of Youth Assembly nominees submitted according to procedures Overall delegation the ambassador will bring to the next Youth Assembly session This means simply being selected as an ambassador does not automatically guarantee outstanding recognition. Performance throughout the ambassador term is an important factor. How to Apply for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program The application process consists of two steps . Step 1: Written Application Interested candidates must first complete and submit the application form for consideration. Applicants should provide information demonstrating that they meet the required qualifications and have the experience, motivation and skills needed to serve as an ambassador. Step 2: Online Interview Shortlisted candidates will proceed to an online interview. Only candidates who are shortlisted will receive an interview request from the AFS Youth Assembly staff. If the interview is successful, selected candidates will receive further information and instructions. First-Come, First-Serve Application Review Applicants should pay particular attention to the way applications will be reviewed. The program states that applications will be reviewed on a first-come, first-serve basis . The first 200 applications will be prioritized . Applications submitted after the first 200 may be placed on a waitlist and reviewed as needed. This makes early application particularly important. Candidates who meet the eligibility requirements should not necessarily wait until the deadline to submit their application. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program is September 18, 2026 . Applicants should submit their application before the deadline and, importantly, consider applying early because the first 200 applications are prioritized. Who Should Consider Applying? The opportunity may be particularly suitable for previous AFS Youth Assembly delegates who are already active in their schools, universities, communities or youth organizations. Strong candidates are likely to be young people who can demonstrate a combination of: Previous AFS Youth Assembly participation Youth leadership experience Community engagement SDG knowledge and experience Commitment to youth empowerment Communication skills Social media experience Content creation abilities Organizational and coordination skills Initiative and problem-solving ability Interest in representing a global youth platform Applicants with fundraising or sponsorship development experience may have an additional advantage because the program identifies this experience as a plus. Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable for Young Leaders The Ambassador Program can be particularly valuable for young people who want to build a stronger international leadership profile. Rather than participating only as a delegate, ambassadors take on an ongoing responsibility to represent and promote the Youth Assembly. This can provide experience in areas such as: Leadership Ambassadors are responsible for promoting programs, engaging other young people and representing the Youth Assembly. Public Communication Speaking at events and participating in media activities can help ambassadors develop their communication and public-speaking abilities. Digital Communication Social media and content creation experience can be strengthened through practical promotional activities. Networking Ambassadors can expand their professional and youth leadership networks. SDG Engagement The role provides an opportunity to remain actively engaged with the Sustainable Development Goals and youth-led development initiatives. Community Impact By nominating young people and promoting Youth Assembly programs, ambassadors can help create opportunities for other young people in their communities. Tips for Potential Applicants Candidates preparing their application should ensure that they can clearly demonstrate the requirements stated by the program. Highlight Your Previous Youth Assembly Experience Because previous participation as a Youth Assembly delegate is required, make this experience clear in your application. Demonstrate Community Engagement Explain your current role in your school, university, organization or community and provide concrete examples of activities you have undertaken. Show Your SDG Experience Do not simply state that you are interested in the SDGs. Demonstrate how you have worked on or contributed to SDG-related activities. Highlight Your Digital Skills If you have created social media campaigns, short videos, TikTok content, blogs or other digital materials, highlight this experience. Demonstrate Initiative Provide examples that show you can independently identify opportunities, solve problems and take action. Emphasize Communication Skills The ambassador role involves communicating with different audiences, so examples of public speaking, coordination, media engagement or community outreach can strengthen your application. Apply Early Because the first 200 applications are prioritized, submitting early is particularly important. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The 2027 AFS Youth Assembly Ambassador Program provides previous Youth Assembly delegates with an opportunity to move beyond participation and take on an active leadership and representation role. Successful ambassadors serve for one year and help disseminate information about AFS Youth Assembly programs, nominate young people to become delegates, participate in promotional activities and represent the Youth Assembly within their communities and wider networks. The program is particularly suited to young leaders who are active in their schools, communities or organizations, have experience with the Sustainable Development Goals, understand youth empowerment and possess strong communication and social media skills. Selected ambassadors can benefit from recognition, networking, professional development, potential speaking opportunities, opportunities to attend Youth Assemblies, online publishing opportunities and other forms of engagement, subject to applicable conditions. One of the most important points for prospective applicants is that applications are reviewed on a first-come, first-served basis, with the first 200 applications prioritized . Therefore, eligible previous AFS Youth Assembly delegates should consider submitting their application well before the September 18, 2026 deadline . For young leaders who want to continue contributing to the AFS Youth Assembly community while developing their leadership, communication and professional networks, the Ambassador Program offers a meaningful way to represent and advance youth participation on a global platform. title: Harvard Takemi Program in International Health 2027–2028: Fully Focused Research Fellowship for Mid-Career Global Health Professionals
summary: The Takemi Program in International Health at Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health is accepting applications for its 2027–2028 fellowship year , offering mid-career health professionals and researchers an opportunity to spend an academic year at Harvard developing an independent research project, strengthening their research capacity, and advancing their leadership in international health. The program is particularly relevant to professionals working on health systems, global health, health policy, health financing, disease prevention and control, health equity, public health, and other challenges involving the mobilization and allocation of limited resources for better health outcomes . Applications for the 2027–2028 program are currently open, and the official deadline is December 31, 2026, at midnight EST (USA) . About the Harvard Takemi Program in International Health The Takemi Program in International Health is an interdisciplinary research and leadership program at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health . The program brings a small group of mid-career health professionals and scholars to Harvard for an academic year to conduct focused research and develop their capacity for research and leadership. The program s central focus is on understanding how limited resources can be mobilized, allocated, and managed to improve health and health systems. Its research has a strong emphasis on practical health challenges, particularly in low- and middle-income countries . Since its establishment in 1983, the program has developed a large international network of Takemi Fellows. Harvard currently reports that more than 330 fellows from more than 60 countries have participated in the program. The program was named after Dr. Taro Takemi , a distinguished Japanese physician-scientist who served as president of the Japan Medical Association for more than two decades. What Is the Takemi Fellowship? The Takemi Program is designed for mid-career researchers and health professionals who have already developed substantial professional and research experience and want to dedicate an academic year to advancing a specific research project. Unlike a conventional degree program, the Takemi Program is centered on an individual research project. Each fellow works with a Harvard faculty advisor and uses the fellowship year to: Develop and conduct a focused research project Analyze existing data Strengthen research methodology Engage with Harvard faculty and researchers Participate in weekly academic seminars Present research findings and receive feedback Develop a publication-quality research paper Strengthen leadership capacity Build international professional networks Explore relevant Harvard coursework and academic resources The program is conducted in person in Boston and does not offer a remote fellowship option. Who Is the Takemi Program Designed For? The program is primarily intended for mid-career health professionals and researchers . Applicants should not view this as a typical early-career fellowship or a postgraduate degree scholarship. Harvard specifically describes the program as being for professionals and researchers who already have an advanced degree, significant work and research experience, publications, and demonstrated leadership potential. Potential applicants may come from areas such as: Public health Medicine Pharmacy Nursing Epidemiology Health economics Health policy Health systems Global health Health administration Nutrition Health financing Disease prevention and control Implementation science Health services research Social and behavioral sciences Other fields relevant to international health The most important consideration is not simply the applicant s professional title. The proposed research should fit the program s broader focus on improving health and health systems through better use of resources, stronger policies, and evidence-based interventions. What Makes the Takemi Program Different? The Takemi Program is particularly valuable because it provides fellows with something that can be difficult to obtain while working full-time: dedicated time and an academic environment to focus intensively on research . Harvard describes the program as providing fellows with the space, time, and flexibility to enhance their research and leadership capacity. Rather than requiring fellows to complete a conventional curriculum, the program allows them to concentrate on a research project that is relevant to their professional work and future contribution to health policy or practice. This makes the program especially relevant for professionals who already have a research question, access to data, and a clear idea of how their research could contribute to improving health systems or policy. Research Focus of the Takemi Program The program s research emphasis is broad but strongly connected to real-world international health challenges. Research can examine questions related to: Health Systems Projects may investigate how health systems are organized, financed, managed, or improved. Health Policy Applicants may explore policies affecting health outcomes, healthcare delivery, access, equity, financing, or population health. Health Resource Allocation A central theme of the program is understanding how scarce resources can be allocated more effectively to achieve better health outcomes. Disease Prevention and Control Research may focus on strategies for preventing, controlling, or managing important diseases and health threats. Health Promotion Projects may examine interventions designed to improve population health and encourage healthier behaviors. Global Health The program is particularly interested in major health challenges affecting low- and middle-income countries and approaches that can produce practical improvements. Health Equity Research examining inequalities, access to healthcare, marginalized populations, and equitable distribution of health resources may also fit within the program s broader research priorities. Harvard states that Takemi research has a strong practical emphasis and that projects should be closely connected to action and to the fellow s work after returning home. A Critical Requirement: Your Data Must Already Be Available One of the most important requirements for prospective applicants is that their research project must be ready for analysis before the fellowship begins. Takemi does not support active data collection during the fellowship. Harvard explicitly states that fellows are expected to conduct their research using data they bring with them and that having the necessary data collected before the program begins is mandatory. This means applicants should not propose a research project that depends on spending the fellowship year conducting extensive surveys, recruiting participants, collecting laboratory samples, or otherwise gathering primary data. Instead, a strong proposal should demonstrate that: The research question has already been defined. The necessary data are available. The applicant has access to the data. The data are sufficiently prepared for analysis. The proposed methodology can realistically be implemented during the fellowship year. The research can result in a publication-quality paper. This requirement is particularly important when designing the research proposal. Faculty Supervision and Research Mentorship Each selected fellow is matched with a Harvard faculty advisor based on the fellow s background and proposed research. Applicants do not need to independently secure a Harvard faculty supervisor before applying. Harvard explains that fellows are matched with faculty mentors after selection based on their background and proposed research. The faculty advisor provides guidance and feedback throughout the research process. Fellows also receive guidance from the Takemi Program leadership and benefit from interactions with other fellows and the broader Harvard community. Weekly Takemi Seminar Series An important component of the program is the weekly Takemi Seminar Series . The seminars expose fellows to a broad range of research topics, methodologies, and perspectives through presentations by Harvard faculty and distinguished visiting scholars. The seminars also create opportunities for discussion and intellectual exchange between fellows, faculty, and invited speakers. This means the fellowship is not simply an individual research residency. Fellows become part of an academic community where they can receive feedback, exchange ideas, and learn from researchers working on different international health challenges. Research Presentations During the Fellowship Takemi Fellows are expected to present their research progress during the fellowship. According to Harvard, fellows participate in: Preliminary presentations Mid-year presentations Final presentations Final academic poster presentation These presentations provide opportunities for fellows to receive feedback from faculty advisors and peers as they develop their research. By the end of the fellowship, fellows are expected to produce a final paper of publishable quality and a research poster. Opportunity to Audit Harvard Courses Although the Takemi Program is primarily a research fellowship, fellows may also have opportunities to audit classes at Harvard Chan School . They are also encouraged to attend Harvard Chan seminars and other academic events. This can allow fellows to supplement their research experience with additional academic exposure based on their professional and research interests. Fellowship Duration The Takemi Program is a full academic-year fellowship . Harvard states that the fellowship runs from: August 1 through June 30 Fellows are expected to arrive before the program orientation, which takes place in late August. The certificate ceremony is generally held in early May. Applicants should therefore plan for a substantial period of residence in Boston rather than treating the fellowship as a short-term visiting researcher position. What Applicants Need to Submit The application includes several components designed to assess the applicant s academic background, professional experience, research capacity, motivation, and leadership potential. The application requires the following: 1. Eligibility Questionnaire Applicants must complete the program s eligibility questionnaire. This helps establish whether the applicant meets the fundamental requirements for consideration. 2. Proof of English Language Proficiency Applicants must provide evidence of English proficiency. The application accepts: TOEFL IELTS Applicants who attended a university where English was the language of instruction may submit a copy of their transcript as evidence, according to the application instructions provided. 3. Statement of Interest The Statement of Interest is an important component of the application. Applicants should explain: Why they are interested in the Takemi Program Why the fellowship is important at this stage of their career How the program will contribute to their professional development What they can contribute to the Takemi community Why they believe they would succeed in the program What they hope to gain from the fellowship What they plan to do after completing the program A strong statement should connect the applicant s past experience, current research interests, Takemi fellowship objectives, and future professional plans . 4. Basic Information Applicants will provide standard personal and application information through the online application portal. 5. Education and Professional Experience Applicants must provide information about their academic and professional background. This section allows the program to understand the applicant s progression and experience in relation to the fellowship. 6. Curriculum Vitae Applicants must upload a current CV in PDF format. The CV should clearly present relevant: Academic qualifications Professional experience Research experience Publications Leadership roles Awards and recognition Relevant projects Professional activities Because the Takemi Program is designed for mid-career professionals, the CV should clearly demonstrate the applicant s professional trajectory and research accomplishments. 7. Research Proposal The research proposal is arguably one of the most important components of the application. Applicants must submit a research proposal of no more than five pages , excluding the title page and references. The proposal should be: Single-spaced 12-point Times New Roman Submitted as a PDF The proposal should include the following sections. Title Page The title page should clearly identify the proposed research project. Summary of the Proposed Project The summary should provide a concise overview of the research, including: The central research problem Specific aims and objectives Potential significance of the research The application guidance suggests approximately half a page for this section. Specific Aims Applicants should clearly explain what the research intends to accomplish. The suggested length is approximately half a page to one page. Background and Significance This section should establish: What is already known What problem remains Why the problem matters Why the proposed research is important How the project contributes to existing knowledge Data Sources Applicants should identify the data that will be used. This is particularly important because the program requires the necessary data to already be collected before the fellowship begins. Research Design and Methods This section should explain how the research will be conducted. Applicants should clearly describe: Research design Analytical approach Variables or measures Methods Data analysis Any relevant methodological considerations The application guidance suggests approximately two pages for this section. References The proposal should conclude with relevant references. 8. Publication List Applicants must provide a list of their publications. This requirement reflects the program s emphasis on applicants who already have demonstrated research experience and scholarly output. Applicants should ensure that the publication list is accurate, clearly organized, and consistent with the CV. 9. Published Document in English Applicants must provide a document published in English. This gives the selection committee an opportunity to assess the applicant s ability to communicate scholarly work in English. 10. Three References Applicants must provide the names and contact information of three referees . After the application is submitted, referees receive an automated request to submit their references to the Takemi Program. Applicants should therefore choose referees who can provide meaningful evidence of their: Research ability Professional experience Leadership potential Academic development Contribution to health systems or policy Capacity to benefit from the fellowship Who Is Eligible for the Takemi Program? Harvard s current application guidance states that applicants should be mid-career researchers and professionals who have: Completed an advanced degree Significant work experience Significant research experience Publications in internationally recognized journals Demonstrated potential for leadership in their home countries Appropriate preparation to benefit from the program Strong English-language ability The program is primarily designed for people who are already established in their professional careers rather than recent graduates. Is the Takemi Program Open to International Applicants? Yes. The Takemi Program is explicitly international and brings together professionals and researchers from around the world. Harvard s historical fellowship network includes fellows from countries across: Africa Asia Europe The Middle East North America South America Other regions Harvard describes the program as having a particular emphasis on fellows from low- and middle-income countries . Therefore, the opportunity is not restricted to U.S. citizens or residents. Professionals from eligible countries around the world can apply if they meet the program s academic, professional, research, and leadership requirements. Is There a Race or Ethnicity Requirement? The program does not specify a racial or ethnic eligibility restriction . Its emphasis is instead on professional background, research experience, leadership potential, English proficiency, and the relevance and quality of the proposed research. Harvard also states that the Takemi Program welcomes research examining issues related to racism, discrimination, marginalization, structural inequality, and other related issues when relevant to international health research. Preference for Low- and Middle-Income Countries The Takemi Program has a longstanding commitment to strengthening research and leadership capacity among professionals from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) . Harvard states that the program has historically focused on building the capacity of mid-career researchers from LMICs and that most Takemi Fellows have focused their work on LMIC-related challenges. This makes the program particularly relevant for professionals whose work addresses health challenges in developing and emerging economies. Financial Support and Funding Applicants should pay close attention to funding arrangements. The Takemi Program states that incoming fellows are generally responsible for securing funding to support their fellowship year. Boston is an expensive city, and Harvard encourages accepted candidates to plan carefully for the cost of living and other expenses. However, limited funding mechanisms are available. For example, Harvard reports that a contribution from the Japan Pharmaceutical Manufacturers Association (JPMA) provides partial financial support for up to two fellows from low-income countries each year. Candidates can indicate their interest in this support during the application process. Importantly, applicants should not assume that the Takemi fellowship automatically provides full funding for the entire year . Accepted applicants may need to secure funding through other sources, such as: Employer or professional development funding Government funding Research grants International fellowships Fulbright funding Other external funding sources Harvard provides information about potential external funding sources for incoming fellows. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027–2028 Takemi Program in International Health is: December 31, 2026 Applications must be submitted by midnight EST (USA) on December 31, 2026. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day because the application includes multiple documents, a research proposal, English-language documentation, publications, and three references. Click HERE to read more and apply. Conclusion The Harvard Takemi Program in International Health 2027–2028 represents a significant opportunity for experienced health professionals and researchers seeking dedicated time to conduct high-quality research, strengthen their leadership capacity, and contribute to better health policies and systems. The program is particularly relevant to mid-career professionals with advanced degrees, substantial research and professional experience, international publications, and demonstrated leadership potential . Its strong emphasis on practical research makes it especially suitable for applicants whose work addresses health challenges in low- and middle-income countries. The program is also international rather than restricted to U.S. applicants, making it potentially relevant to qualified health professionals and researchers across Africa, Asia, Latin America, the Middle East, Europe, and other regions . Harvard s fellowship network demonstrates its longstanding international reach. The application deadline is December 31, 2026, at midnight EST (USA). Applicants should begin preparing well in advance because the application requires a research proposal, statement of interest, CV, publication list, English-language documentation, writing sample, and three references. title: NASA Spring 2027 OSTEM Internships: Apply for Paid NASA Internship Opportunities Before September 14, 2026
summary: NASA has opened applications for its Spring 2027 Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) Internship Program , offering students the opportunity to gain hands-on experience by contributing to real NASA projects and working alongside NASA professionals. For students interested in science, technology, engineering, mathematics, space exploration, aeronautics, research, communications, business, and other fields relevant to NASA s mission , the OSTEM program can provide valuable practical experience, professional development, and exposure to one of the world s leading space and science organizations. The application deadline for the Spring 2027 NASA OSTEM Internships is September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time . Applicants should therefore review available opportunities, confirm their eligibility, prepare their application materials, and submit their applications before the deadline. About the NASA OSTEM Internship Program NASA s Office of STEM Engagement (OSTEM) runs internship opportunities designed to give students practical experience connected to NASA s missions. According to NASA, the OSTEM program provides students with short-term, hands-on opportunities to work on real NASA projects . Interns can develop technical and professional skills while receiving guidance and mentorship from NASA personnel. NASA provides more than 2,000 students annually with opportunities through its OSTEM internship program. The program is therefore more than a conventional academic internship. Selected students have the opportunity to gain experience in a professional environment and contribute to projects connected to NASA s broader work in science, technology, aeronautics, and space exploration. What Is the Spring 2027 NASA OSTEM Internship? The Spring 2027 OSTEM internship is part of NASA s annual internship cycle. NASA operates three major OSTEM internship sessions each year: Spring Summer Fall For the Spring 2027 cycle, applications must be submitted by September 14, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET . The spring and fall OSTEM internships generally run for approximately 15 weeks , while summer internships generally last around 10 weeks. What Do NASA OSTEM Interns Do? NASA OSTEM interns work on projects that contribute to the agency s mission. Depending on the specific internship, responsibilities can vary considerably. NASA offers opportunities across a broad range of academic and professional disciplines. Interns may have the opportunity to: Work on real NASA projects Conduct research and analysis Support scientific or engineering activities Develop technical solutions Analyze data Assist with communications and outreach Contribute to technology development Work with NASA scientists, engineers, researchers, and other professionals Develop professional and workplace skills Gain practical experience related to their academic field Participate in a professional NASA work environment Importantly, NASA states that its internship opportunities are not limited exclusively to STEM majors . NASA also offers opportunities for students from non-STEM disciplines, depending on the available projects and NASA s workforce needs. This means students should not automatically assume that they are ineligible simply because their degree is not in engineering, physics, computer science, or another traditional STEM discipline. Key Benefits of a NASA OSTEM Internship A NASA internship can provide several important benefits for students seeking to build their academic and professional careers. 1. Gain Hands-On Professional Experience One of the major advantages of the OSTEM program is the opportunity to move beyond classroom learning. Interns can work on projects and activities that provide practical experience and help them understand how their academic knowledge can be applied in a professional environment. 2. Work on Real NASA Projects OSTEM internships are designed around actual NASA projects rather than purely theoretical assignments. Students can contribute to work related to NASA s broader mission in areas such as science, technology, aeronautics, and space exploration. 3. Learn From NASA Professionals Interns have the opportunity to work with NASA experts and mentors. This can expose students to professional approaches to: Research Problem-solving Project management Technical work Communication Collaboration Innovation 4. Strengthen Your Resume Having hands-on experience with NASA can be a valuable addition to a student s academic and professional profile. The experience can demonstrate exposure to: Professional project environments Research or technical work Team collaboration Problem-solving Innovation Mission-oriented work Students can subsequently use the experience when applying for graduate programmes, scholarships, research opportunities, jobs, and other internships. 5. Develop Technical and Professional Skills NASA describes OSTEM internships as opportunities to build both technical skills and career readiness . Depending on the project, students may develop skills related to their discipline while also strengthening transferable skills such as communication, teamwork, organization, critical thinking, and professional problem-solving. 6. Explore Careers at NASA An OSTEM internship can also help students understand what it is like to work within NASA and explore potential career paths. For students interested in eventually pursuing careers in aerospace, science, engineering, research, technology, communications, administration, or other NASA-related fields, an internship can provide useful exposure to the organization. Who Can Apply for the NASA OSTEM Internship? NASA s current eligibility requirements specify that OSTEM candidates must meet several requirements. Applicants must: Be a U.S. citizen Be at least 16 years old at the time of application Have a minimum 3.0 cumulative GPA on a 4.0 scale Be a full-time or part-time college student , from undergraduate through graduate level Be enrolled in a degree-granting programme at a U.S. Department of Education-accredited college or university Be studying in a course of study aligned with NASA s needs NASA also indicates that educators who are enrolled as students can be eligible to apply. Students who have recently graduated may also be eligible for internships taking place during the three internship sessions immediately following their graduation, subject to NASA s eligibility requirements. Do You Need to Study a STEM Subject? Not necessarily. The name Office of STEM Engagement might lead some applicants to believe that only STEM students can apply. However, NASA explicitly states that it offers internships for non-STEM majors as well . The key consideration is whether the applicant s academic programme and qualifications align with the requirements of the particular internship opportunity.
