title: Global Fund Business & Consultancy Opportunities 2026: Apply for International Tenders, Consulting Contracts and Global Health Procurement Opportunities
summary: About the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria The Global Fund is an international financing partnership dedicated to accelerating progress against HIV/AIDS, tuberculosis and malaria while supporting stronger and more resilient health systems. Rather than directly implementing most country programs itself, the Global Fund finances programs that are implemented through its partners and Principal Recipients. This distinction is important when reviewing its business opportunities. The organization s Business Consultancy Opportunities page primarily covers procurement undertaken by the Global Fund itself, particularly requirements of its Secretariat. Principal Recipients administering Global Fund grants may conduct their own procurement processes separately in accordance with applicable grant requirements. The Global Fund s procurement activities are intended to support its organizational operations while helping ensure that resources ultimately contribute to effective global health interventions. What Are Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities? The opportunities published through the platform are essentially competitive procurement exercises . Depending on the requirement, the Global Fund may seek proposals from: Individual consultants Consultancy firms Professional service providers Companies Contractors Suppliers Manufacturers Technical organizations Research organizations Specialist agencies Procurement service providers Other qualified entities The Global Fund s Procurement Policy defines a supplier broadly as an external entity that may include an organization, individual contractor or service provider supplying goods, services or other support. Consequently, applicants should not assume that every opportunity is intended for an individual consultant. Some tenders may require established companies or organizations capable of delivering substantial contracts. What Types of Opportunities May Be Available? The exact opportunities change throughout the year. Potential procurement areas can include professional and technical services associated with the Global Fund s operations and mission. Depending on organizational requirements, opportunities may potentially cover areas such as: Global health consulting HIV-related technical services Tuberculosis programs and expertise Malaria-related technical services Health-system strengthening Procurement and supply-chain services Public-health analysis Data and analytics Monitoring and evaluation Independent evaluation Research Strategy development Organizational consulting Finance and accounting services Audit and assurance Risk management Information technology Digital systems Communications Knowledge management Human resources consulting Legal or regulatory support Program management Project management Logistics Procurement of goods Health-product procurement Pharmaceutical products Diagnostic products Other specialized technical or operational services Actual eligibility and technical requirements are determined separately for each solicitation. Global Fund Consulting Opportunities Consultancy assignments represent an important component of the Global Fund s external contracting activities. The Global Fund s careers information confirms that it engages both individual consultants and consultancy firms , with relevant opportunities published through the Business Consultancy Opportunities section. These assignments should not be confused with permanent employment vacancies. Permanent and fixed-term staff vacancies generally appear through the Global Fund s separate careers system, while consulting and supplier procurements are normally handled as contracting opportunities. Consultants may therefore be engaged to deliver specific outputs, technical expertise, analysis, assessments, evaluations or other professional services under contractual terms defined in the relevant solicitation. Global Fund Procurement Opportunities for Suppliers Companies interested in doing business with the Global Fund should understand that procurement is governed by formal institutional rules. The Global Fund states that it seeks value for money in the procurement of goods and services and publishes tenders as part of a transparent procurement process. Its Procurement Policy applies to several areas, including: Procurement of health products and related services through the Pooled Procurement Mechanism. Procurement of goods and services financed through Global Fund operating expenses. Certain other procurements financed through approved investments or funds. Procurement of Local Fund Agent services. This means the procurement framework covers both operational requirements and major elements of the organization s health-product supply system. Open Competition Is the Standard Procurement Approach One of the most important aspects for prospective bidders is the Global Fund s emphasis on competitive procurement. Its Procurement Policy states that procurement should generally be based on effective competition and identifies open competition as the organization s standard procurement method. Effective competition may involve: Publicly advertising procurement opportunities; Inviting a sufficient number of prospective suppliers; Ensuring bidders compete under equivalent conditions; Receiving sufficient independent offers; and Evaluating proposals against established requirements. This approach is intended to provide a transparent and competitive environment for qualified suppliers. Core Global Fund Procurement Principles Prospective applicants should understand the principles against which Global Fund procurement is managed. 1. Value for Money Procurement decisions are not necessarily based solely on selecting the lowest-priced offer. The Global Fund defines value for money by considering the relationship among: Price Quality Performance Total cost of ownership Technical suitability Delivery requirements Organizational capability Environmental, social, sustainability and risk considerations may also be incorporated where relevant. A bidder should therefore ensure that its proposal demonstrates overall value rather than simply offering a low financial price. 2. Effective Competition Competitive procurement is intended to ensure multiple qualified suppliers have a fair opportunity to participate. The organization seeks an adequate competitive environment and normally uses open competition as its standard approach. 3. Fairness, Impartiality and Integrity The Global Fund requires bidders to be treated equally and proposals to be evaluated objectively against predetermined criteria. Its Procurement Policy specifically emphasizes avoiding actual, potential or perceived conflicts of interest. 4. Client-Centered Procurement Procurement is also expected to meet the requirements of the internal Global Fund unit requesting the goods or services. This means suppliers must closely understand the technical specifications and intended outcomes of each tender. 5. Sustainable Procurement The Global Fund explicitly incorporates sustainability into its procurement framework. Its policy states that sustainable procurement seeks to: Reduce environmental impacts across supply chains; Support fair and humane working conditions; Promote social progress; Support economic development; and Contribute to the long-term well-being of communities. 6. Best Interests of the Global Fund Procurement must ultimately support the organization s mission, protect its assets and ensure responsible stewardship of its resources. Ethical Requirements for Global Fund Suppliers Ethical compliance is a major requirement for companies and consultants seeking contracts with the organization. The Global Fund s Code of Conduct for Suppliers applies broadly to bidders, suppliers, agents, intermediaries, consultants and contractors, as well as relevant representatives, employees, subcontractors and affiliates. Suppliers are expected to participate in procurement processes honestly, fairly, transparently and accountably. The organization prohibits practices including: Corruption Fraud Collusion Anti-competitive practices Coercion Misrepresentation Improper payments Undisclosed commissions Other unethical procurement practices Applicants should therefore ensure that every statement, qualification, reference, financial proposal and declaration contained in their bid is accurate. Compliance With Laws Suppliers and their representatives are required to comply with applicable laws and regulations in the countries where they conduct business, as well as relevant Global Fund rules and policies. The Code of Conduct also includes provisions concerning matters such as: Anti-corruption Anti-money laundering Fair competition Responsible use of Global Fund resources Disclosure of conflicts Human rights Labor standards Environmental responsibilities Child protection Protection from sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment These requirements should be treated as substantive contractual obligations rather than formalities. Record-Keeping and Audit Requirements Companies that obtain Global Fund-financed contracts should also be prepared for accountability and audit requirements. The Supplier Code of Conduct requires suppliers to maintain appropriate and complete financial and business records associated with Global Fund-financed contracts for at least five years after the final payment under the contract . Suppliers are also expected to cooperate with the Global Fund, including its Office of the Inspector General , where access to relevant records, documents or personnel is reasonably requested. This requirement is particularly relevant to larger consulting firms, contractors and suppliers managing financially significant contracts. Conflicts of Interest Potential suppliers must pay close attention to conflict-of-interest requirements. The procurement framework seeks to ensure objective evaluation and prevent circumstances where a bidder could obtain an improper competitive advantage. Suppliers should disclose relevant relationships or situations where required and carefully review the specific tender documentation before submitting their proposal. Failure to properly address conflicts may jeopardize a bid or contract. Can Suppliers Use the Global Fund Name or Logo? Winning a Global Fund contract does not automatically authorize a supplier to use the organization s name or logo for advertising. The Supplier Code states that suppliers may not, without prior written consent, use the Global Fund s name or logo in publicity or advertising, represent a business relationship as an endorsement of their products or services, or make statements on behalf of the Global Fund. Companies should therefore obtain appropriate authorization before publicly promoting a contractual relationship. Health Product Procurement Opportunities The Global Fund is also a major procurer of medicines and health products. Its Pooled Procurement Mechanism (PPM) aggregates orders from participating grant implementers to obtain competitive prices and delivery conditions from manufacturers and suppliers. In 2025, the mechanism handled approximately US$1.02 billion in orders for implementing partners in 81 countries . Products available through the mechanism include categories such as: Antiretroviral medicines Antimalarial medicines Other essential medicines Insecticide-treated mosquito nets Viral load tests Rapid diagnostic tests Regular tenders for medicines and diagnostic products may also appear through the Business Consultancy Opportunities section. Important Information for Health Product Suppliers Companies interested specifically in supplying medicines or health products should not rely exclusively on the general tender page. The Global Fund advises potential health-product suppliers to: Review its Procurement Policy. Understand quality-assurance requirements applicable to their products. Review relevant procurement and purchasing information. Understand the Pooled Procurement Mechanism and wambo.org. Review the Code of Conduct for Suppliers. Review applicable procurement regulations. The organization does not maintain a general list of automatically preselected suppliers for implementing partners. Manufacturers must therefore satisfy the particular regulatory, quality and procurement conditions applicable to their products. What Documents Should Applicants Read Before Applying? The Global Fund explicitly advises prospective bidders to review key procurement documentation before submitting a proposal. Important documents include: Procurement Policy Code of Conduct for Suppliers Terms and Conditions for the Purchase of Goods and Services Privacy Statement for the Global Fund Procurement Process Travel Guidelines for Contractors Applicants should not treat these documents as optional background reading. They can establish important conditions relating to: Ethical conduct Contract administration Financial arrangements Confidentiality Travel Compliance Reporting Supplier obligations Legal liability Tender-specific conditions may supplement these general rules. How to Apply for Global Fund Business and Consultancy Opportunities The application procedure is not identical for every procurement. The official Business Consultancy Opportunities page directs applicants to the Global Fund s Open Tenders platform. Each individual solicitation contains its own: Tender description Terms of reference or specifications Eligibility requirements Required qualifications Submission procedure Technical documentation Financial requirements Deadline Contact or clarification procedure Applicants should therefore first identify a tender that matches their qualifications and carefully review the complete tender package before preparing a proposal. View Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities Preparing a Competitive Proposal Although tender requirements vary, applicants should generally prepare to demonstrate why they are technically and commercially capable of delivering the requested work. A strong proposal may need to address areas such as: Understanding of the Assignment Demonstrate a clear understanding of: The Global Fund s requirements Expected outputs Relevant technical issues Contract objectives Deliverables Technical Approach Where required, explain: Proposed methodology Implementation approach Work plan Quality-assurance arrangements Risk management Project governance Reporting arrangements Relevant Experience Applicants may need to demonstrate previous experience delivering similar assignments. Evidence could include: Comparable contracts Client references Case studies Project summaries Past performance Demonstrated international experience Personnel Consultancy tenders may require CVs of proposed experts. Applicants should ensure that each proposed team member clearly satisfies any mandatory: Education requirements Professional qualifications Years of experience Technical competencies Language requirements Financial Proposal Price should be realistic and consistent with the technical methodology. Because Global Fund procurement evaluates overall value for money rather than price alone, applicants should avoid compromising technical quality merely to submit the lowest possible price. Evaluation of Proposals The exact scoring methodology will be provided in the individual tender documentation. However, the Global Fund s overarching Procurement Policy permits consideration of: Technical factors Commercial factors Organizational factors Pricing Environmental factors Social considerations Sustainability Risk Appropriate due diligence Applicants should therefore respond directly to every evaluation criterion instead of submitting a generic corporate proposal. Tender Review and Contract Award The Global Fund s procurement framework includes controls before contracts are awarded. Its Procurement Policy states that procurement contracts are subject to a mandatory review process prior to award to confirm compliance with applicable policies and procurement rules. No award may be made before that review is completed. This reflects the organization s emphasis on transparency, accountability and procurement integrity. Are These Opportunities Based in Geneva? Many opportunities published through this particular portal primarily involve supplying goods or services to the Global Fund Secretariat in Geneva, Switzerland . However, this does not necessarily mean every consultant must permanently reside in Switzerland. Assignment location, travel requirements, remote-working arrangements and geographical eligibility can differ substantially from one tender to another. Applicants should therefore consult the individual Terms of Reference rather than assuming an opportunity is either remote or Geneva-based. Can International Applicants Apply? The Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities page does not establish one universal nationality restriction covering all tenders . It states that open tenders are available for prospective suppliers to review and consider. The Supplier Code also covers a broad range of bidders, suppliers, consultants, contractors, organizations and representatives. However, international eligibility must be determined tender by tender . A specific procurement may impose requirements relating to: Country registration Geographic presence Local expertise Language Tax registration Professional licensing Experience in certain regions Ability to travel Manufacturer authorization Product regulatory approval Applicants should therefore never interpret the general procurement page as guaranteeing eligibility for every nationality in every procurement. Are There Opportunities for Applicants From Africa, Asia, Europe and Other Regions? Potentially, yes, depending on the specific tender. The Global Fund operates globally, and its procurement ecosystem includes international companies, consultants, manufacturers and service providers. But there is no blanket statement on the Business Consultancy Opportunities page saying every tender is universally open to every country . Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, Latin America, the Caribbean, the Middle East and Oceania should check the nationality, registration and location provisions of each individual procurement notice. Application Deadline There is no single overall deadline for Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities. This is an ongoing procurement portal. Each open tender has its own closing date and submission time , which are stated within the individual solicitation documentation. The official page specifically directs applicants to the individual tender for submission instructions and contact information. Applicants should therefore: Open the current tender list. Identify the relevant opportunity. Check its exact closing date. Note the applicable time zone. Submit the complete proposal before the stated deadline. Late submissions may not be accepted under tender-specific rules. Important Difference Between Global Fund Tenders and Global Fund Jobs Applicants should understand that this procurement portal is not the Global Fund s ordinary employment vacancies page . The organization maintains a separate recruitment system for staff vacancies. Its careers page specifically explains that consulting opportunities for consultants and consultancy firms are listed under Business Consultancy Opportunities. Therefore: Permanent or temporary employment: Check Global Fund Careers. Consultancy contracts, supplier opportunities and tenders: Check Business Consultancy Opportunities. This distinction is particularly important for applicants preparing CVs or proposals. Why Consider Global Fund Business Opportunities? Working with the Global Fund can provide experienced consultants and organizations with an opportunity to contribute specialized expertise to one of the world s major global health financing institutions. Potential benefits include: Participation in international health initiatives Exposure to complex global programs Opportunities to work with international stakeholders Experience with major institutional procurement systems Potential long-term professional relationships Opportunities for specialist consulting firms Participation in health-product and supply-chain initiatives Work contributing indirectly to the fight against HIV, tuberculosis and malaria However, applicants should approach these opportunities as formal competitive procurements rather than guaranteed contracts. Tips for Prospective Applicants Before submitting a Global Fund tender, applicants should: Read the complete Terms of Reference or technical specifications. Confirm that all mandatory eligibility criteria can be satisfied. Read the Procurement Policy. Review the Supplier Code of Conduct. Examine the applicable Terms and Conditions. Prepare a proposal specifically tailored to the tender. Demonstrate relevant experience with evidence. Provide qualified personnel where required. Address every evaluation criterion. Ensure pricing is complete and commercially realistic. Disclose potential conflicts where required. Avoid unsupported claims about organizational capacity. Confirm the deadline and applicable time zone. Submit through the method specified in the tender. Retain copies of all documents submitted. Important Warning for Applicants Applicants should use only official Global Fund procurement channels and verify all tender information against the official website. A legitimate procurement process should include formal documentation defining the required goods or services, submission requirements and applicable conditions. Prospective bidders should also remember that winning a Global Fund contract does not provide unrestricted permission to use the organization s name or logo for advertising purposes. Conclusion The Global Fund Business Consultancy Opportunities platform provides an important route for qualified consultants, businesses, manufacturers, contractors and professional service providers seeking to work with an internationally recognized global health financing organization. Unlike a conventional job board, the platform operates as an ongoing competitive procurement system , with individual tenders covering different goods, consulting assignments and specialized services. The Global Fund emphasizes transparency, effective competition, integrity, sustainability and value for money throughout its procurement activities. Applicants should therefore expect rigorous technical, ethical and contractual standards. There is no universal application deadline . Each opportunity has its own closing date, technical requirements, financial requirements and submission procedure. Prospective suppliers and consultants should regularly review the official portal, identify opportunities aligned with their expertise, carefully study all tender documentation and prepare compliant, evidence-based proposals. title: USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program in Washington, D.C.: Applications Open for U.S. Citizens Interested in Public Service, Agriculture, Policy and Rural Development
summary: Applications are now open for the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Spring 2027 Internship Program , offering emerging professionals an opportunity to gain practical experience inside one of the largest departments of the U.S. federal government. The Spring 2027 cohort will run from January 25 through April 30, 2027 , with applications due by November 13, 2026 . The program is an unpaid, in-person volunteer internship based in Washington, D.C. USDA does not provide housing or relocation assistance. Unlike many internships that are limited to currently enrolled university students, USDA s current Internship Program does not require applicants to be enrolled in school or to hold a college degree . According to USDA s official FAQ, applicants must be U.S. citizens and at least 18 years old at the time of application . Candidates from a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds may therefore be considered. The program provides participants with direct exposure to public service and federal government operations while allowing them to contribute to work related to agriculture, food systems, conservation, rural communities, communications, research, public policy, stakeholder engagement and other areas central to USDA s mission. About the USDA Internship Program The U.S. Department of Agriculture describes its Internship Program as a public-service and leadership-development experience intended to introduce emerging leaders to USDA s work and help prepare them for careers in public service, agriculture, science, policy and community development. USDA s mission reaches far beyond farming alone. The Department works across areas including: Agriculture and agricultural markets Food and nutrition Food safety Rural economic development Natural-resource conservation Forestry and environmental stewardship Agricultural research Data and economics International agricultural trade Communications Public policy Congressional relations Civil rights Community partnerships Stakeholder engagement Interns may therefore have opportunities to work in areas aligned with a broad range of academic interests, professional skills and career ambitions. USDA states that interns may contribute to activities such as research, program operations, data analysis, communications, outreach and stakeholder engagement. Exact responsibilities depend on the mission area or staff office in which an intern is placed. Spring 2027 USDA Internship Dates The current application is specifically for the Spring 2027 cohort . Program period: January 25, 2027 – April 30, 2027 Application deadline: November 13, 2026 USDA s application information states that applicants should be available during the program period. The application form itself also allows candidates with limited availability to explain their circumstances, although applicants should expect the program to require substantial in-person participation. Applicants should therefore carefully consider academic, employment, transportation and housing commitments before applying. Is the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Paid? No. The current USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program is explicitly described as an unpaid volunteer internship . Applicants will not receive a salary from USDA through this program. This distinction is important because USDA also operates other student employment initiatives, including Pathways opportunities, some of which may be paid. The internship advertised on the USDA page linked above, however, is the USDA Volunteer Internship Program and is unpaid. USDA encourages applicants to explore whether their educational institutions or relevant nonprofit organizations can provide funding or academic support. Applicants should also be aware that outside income, funding or housing assistance associated with the internship may require prior approval from USDA. Housing and Relocation Assistance USDA does not provide housing specifically for interns under this program. Participants are responsible for finding and paying for their own accommodation for the duration of the internship. USDA also states on the Spring 2027 application page that the program provides no housing or relocation assistance . Candidates who do not already live within commuting distance of Washington, D.C., should therefore calculate expected costs before accepting an internship, including: Housing Transportation Meals Local commuting Relocation expenses Personal living expenses Because the position is unpaid, financial planning will be particularly important for applicants relocating to Washington. Internship Location: Washington, D.C. The USDA Internship Program is conducted in person in Washington, D.C. Interns are expected to work onsite at USDA s Whitten Building , where they participate directly in departmental operations and interact with USDA personnel. USDA specifically states that remote participation is not available for this program. Applicants should therefore not apply on the assumption that they will be permitted to complete the internship remotely from another U.S. state or another country. Expected Internship Schedule and Working Hours Most USDA internships under this program operate on a Monday-to-Friday schedule , typically within approximately 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. Some flexibility may be available for interns who have academic or other program requirements. USDA states that interns considered full-time are generally expected to work the equivalent of approximately 4.5 days per week , although limited adjustments may be permitted where appropriate. Applicants should therefore view the opportunity as a substantial professional commitment rather than a few-hours-per-week volunteer placement. What Will USDA Interns Do? Specific duties will depend heavily on the intern s assigned mission area or staff office. USDA identifies potential internship activities including: Conducting research Supporting program operations Analyzing data Drafting communications Assisting with outreach activities Supporting stakeholder engagement Developing briefing materials Supporting meetings and events Conducting policy-related research Helping coordinate projects Participating in departmental programming This structure allows interns to gain practical experience while contributing to ongoing federal government activities. Leadership and Professional Development The program is not intended to consist solely of administrative assignments. USDA describes it as a leadership-development and public-service experience designed to help young and emerging professionals better understand federal service. Interns participate in department-wide programming, including lunch-and-learn sessions featuring USDA leaders and subject-matter experts . Through these activities, interns may gain exposure to: Federal decision-making Government leadership Agriculture and food policy Public administration Interagency operations Stakeholder engagement Professional networking Career development Public-service culture USDA Mission Areas and Offices Available to Applicants As part of the application, candidates must list their top three preferred USDA Mission Areas or Staff Offices . USDA s official Office Opportunities document identifies a wide range of potential placement areas. 1. Farm Production and Conservation Farm Production and Conservation (FPAC) serves as a major focal point for farmers, ranchers and other stewards of private agricultural and forest lands. Its work includes programs related to: Crop insurance Agricultural conservation Farm safety nets Lending Disaster programs Risk mitigation for agricultural producers This area may be particularly relevant for applicants interested in agricultural economics, environmental policy, farming systems, risk management or public administration. 2. Food and Nutrition Administration The Food and Nutrition Administration focuses on reducing food insecurity and improving nutrition security in the United States. Its work includes administration of federal domestic nutrition-assistance programs as well as science-based nutrition guidance, policy coordination and nutrition education. This area may appeal to applicants interested in food security, nutrition, social policy, public health or program management. 3. Food Safety and Inspection Service The Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) is USDA s public-health agency responsible for helping ensure the safety of meat, poultry and egg products. Its work includes food-safety oversight and implementation of federal laws governing meat, poultry, egg products and humane animal handling. Students and professionals interested in food science, public health, veterinary science, regulatory policy or compliance may find this mission area particularly relevant. 4. Marketing and Regulatory Programs Marketing and Regulatory Programs (MRP) supports domestic and international agricultural markets while protecting U.S. plant and animal health. Its responsibilities include: Agricultural marketing Plant health Animal health Biotechnology regulation Animal-welfare administration Wildlife-damage management Participation in national and international standards development 5. Research, Education and Economics The Research, Education and Economics (REE) mission area supports research, analysis and education related to a safe, competitive and sustainable U.S. food and agricultural system. Its work also addresses communities, families and young people. Applicants interested in science, statistics, economics, research, data analysis or education may find REE especially relevant. 6. Rural Development USDA Rural Development supports rural communities through loans, grants and loan-guarantee programs. Its work includes investments relating to: High-speed internet Electricity Transportation infrastructure Businesses Healthcare Education Housing Community facilities This placement could be highly relevant for students of economics, finance, infrastructure, public policy, community development or business administration. 7. Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs Trade and Foreign Agricultural Affairs (TFAA) works to expand international opportunities for American farmers and ranchers. Its responsibilities include international agricultural trade policy, market intelligence, trade promotion and export development. USDA s Foreign Agricultural Service maintains a global network covering numerous countries, while the U.S. Codex Office coordinates American participation in international food-standard setting. This area may be particularly attractive to applicants interested in international relations, economics, trade, diplomacy, agriculture or global food policy. 8. Natural Resources and Environment The Natural Resources and Environment (NRE) mission area focuses on maintaining the health, diversity and productivity of U.S. forests and grasslands. It works with states, tribes and communities across the country to steward natural resources. Applicants with interests in environmental studies, forestry, climate policy, conservation, sustainability or natural-resource management may consider this placement. USDA Staff Offices Offering Internship Exposure Applicants can also express preferences for USDA staff offices. Office of the Secretary The Office of the Secretary provides leadership and strategic direction across USDA. Interns may support: High-level policy coordination Research Briefing materials Departmental decision-making Senior leadership meetings Major events This placement provides particularly close exposure to senior-level federal policy and executive decision-making. White House Liaison Office The White House Liaison Office connects USDA with the Executive Office of the President. Its responsibilities include personnel matters, political appointments, leadership onboarding and coordination with the White House. Interns may assist with research, personnel processes, organizational analysis, briefings and leadership engagements. Office of Communications The Office of Communications manages public information and strategic communication across USDA. Internship work may involve: Writing and editing Press support Briefing materials Digital content Media monitoring Event support Visual storytelling Strategic messaging It may be particularly suitable for applicants interested in journalism, public relations, communications, digital media or public affairs. Office of Congressional Relations The Office of Congressional Relations acts as USDA s main liaison with the U.S. House of Representatives and Senate. Interns may gain experience in: Legislative research Tracking congressional hearings Monitoring legislation Preparing background materials Congressional communications Supporting departmental engagements with lawmakers Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights The Office of the Assistant Secretary for Civil Rights (OASCR) leads USDA s work relating to civil-rights compliance and equal treatment. Potential intern activities include: Civil-rights policy research Data analysis Training-material preparation Outreach Compliance-related work Office of Partnerships and Public Engagement The Office of Partnerships and Public Engagement (OPPE) works with rural and underserved communities and helps connect stakeholders with USDA programs and resources. Interns may assist with: Outreach strategy Partnership development Community-needs research Event coordination Stakeholder engagement materials Who Can Apply? One of the distinctive features of the current USDA internship is its relatively broad educational eligibility. According to USDA: Applicants must be at least 18 years old . Applicants must be U.S. citizens . Applicants do not need to be currently enrolled in school. Applicants do not need to hold a college degree. People from a wide range of educational and professional backgrounds may apply. The online application provides education-status options including: Currently enrolled in high school Currently enrolled in college or university Recently graduated Not currently enrolled in school This confirms that the program is not restricted solely to university students. Does an Applicant Need a Specific Major? No specific academic major is identified as a universal requirement for the program. The application nevertheless asks candidates to identify their major or field of study , where applicable. Applicants who are not currently enrolled may provide their most recent field of study or indicate that the question is not applicable. Given USDA s broad responsibilities, potentially relevant backgrounds include—but are not limited to: Agriculture Agricultural economics Economics Finance Business administration Public administration Public policy Political science International relations Law Communications Journalism Data science Statistics Computer science Food science Nutrition Public health Environmental science Forestry Biology Animal sciences Rural development Sociology Community development Applicants should choose office preferences that align logically with their interests, abilities and professional goals. Is a Minimum GPA Required? The application asks candidates to provide a GPA, but USDA marks the GPA field as optional . The current program page therefore does not establish a universal minimum GPA requirement for the Spring 2027 Volunteer Internship Program. USDA Internship Application Requirements The application must be submitted through USDA s official online portal. Hard-copy applications sent by mail are not accepted . Applicants will need to complete several sections. Section 1: Personal Information Applicants provide details including: Full name Street address City, state and ZIP code Telephone number Email address Section 2: Education Applicants indicate their education status and provide applicable details such as: Current school or university Major or field of study Expected graduation date GPA, if they choose to provide it Section 3: Spring 2027 Availability Applicants must indicate whether they are available for the full Spring 2027 semester or have limited availability. Candidates selecting limited availability must provide an explanation. Section 4: Statement of Interest The application requires substantive written responses addressing several topics. Applicants are asked to explain: Why they are interested in an internship with USDA. What skills and experiences they could bring to USDA. Which issues affecting agriculture, food systems, conservation or rural communities they want to learn more about and why. What public service means to them and how they have demonstrated commitment to their community. A personal accomplishment they are proud of and how it shaped their perspective on success. The application also asks whether applicants have previously volunteered or worked for a: Political campaign Elected official Government official Applicants answering yes are asked to describe their role and the relevant campaign, office or official as well as the year or years involved. Importantly, USDA states separately that political preference is not used as a deciding factor in internship application review . Section 5: Office Preferences Candidates must identify their top three USDA Mission Areas or Staff Offices where they would prefer to intern. Applicants should research these offices before selecting preferences because their choices can help communicate their career interests and indicate where their skills may best fit USDA s needs. Section 6: References Applicants must provide at least two references who can discuss their: Qualifications Character Work ethic Commitment to public service USDA suggests potential references such as: Professors Supervisors Mentors Community leaders Applicants should provide complete contact information for each reference. Recommendation letters are optional and may be uploaded as PDF documents if applicants wish to include them. All required reference information must be submitted by the application deadline. USDA notes that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis , which makes early submission advisable. Resume Requirement Applicants must upload a resume. The application portal currently accepts: PDF DOC DOCX The maximum upload size shown on the application form is 20 MB . Candidates should tailor their resume to demonstrate relevant experience rather than using a generic resume whenever possible. Useful information may include: Education Work experience Volunteer experience Leadership activities Community involvement Research projects Public-service activities Relevant technical skills Communication skills Data or analytical experience Policy experience Agriculture, food or environmental interests How Applicants Can Strengthen Their Application Because the program seeks individuals interested in public service, candidates should demonstrate more than academic achievement alone. Strong applications should provide concrete evidence of: Interest in USDA s mission Commitment to public service Community involvement Leadership Initiative Research or analytical skills Communication ability Professional maturity Interest in agriculture, food systems, conservation or rural communities When answering the statement-of-interest questions, applicants should avoid vague claims such as I am passionate about agriculture. Instead, they should explain why a particular issue matters to them, what they have already done in that area, what they hope to learn and how USDA experience fits their longer-term professional objectives. Political Experience and Political Preference Applicants are specifically asked whether they have worked or volunteered for a political campaign, elected official or government official. However, USDA states that political preference itself is not considered in the application review process . Applicants should answer the application questions accurately and transparently. What matters is their ability to demonstrate commitment to USDA s public-service mission and responsibilities toward farmers, rural communities and the American public. Important Financial Considerations Before Applying Because the Spring 2027 internship is unpaid and based in Washington, D.C., candidates should evaluate the financial implications carefully. Before applying or accepting an offer, consider: Whether you can live in or commute to Washington, D.C., from January through April 2027. Whether your college or university can provide academic credit or financial assistance. Whether you qualify for support from an external nonprofit organization. Your housing costs. Transportation and commuting costs. Food and personal expenses. Whether outside funding would require USDA approval. The absence of compensation does not diminish the professional exposure available through the program, but applicants should make a realistic financial assessment before committing. Why Consider the USDA Spring 2027 Internship? The program may be particularly valuable for individuals interested in understanding how federal institutions operate in practice. Participants may gain firsthand exposure to: Federal public administration Agricultural policymaking Policy research Data analysis Rural-development programs Food and nutrition programs Environmental conservation International agricultural trade Congressional relations Communications Civil-rights compliance Community engagement Executive-branch operations Because internship placements span both policy-focused and operational offices, the program can be relevant to candidates from many academic and professional backgrounds. The experience may also help applicants determine whether a longer-term career in public service, agriculture, federal policy or related sectors is appropriate for them. Application Deadline The official deadline for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program is November 13, 2026 . USDA notes that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, so interested candidates should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their materials. How to Apply for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Applications must be submitted electronically through the official USDA Internship Application portal. Apply for the USDA Spring 2027 Internship Applicants can review the main program information here: USDA Internship Program Official Website Before submitting, candidates should make sure they have: Completed all personal and educational information. Confirmed their Spring 2027 availability. Prepared strong responses to the statement-of-interest questions. Selected three preferred USDA mission areas or offices. Provided two appropriate references with current contact information. Prepared an updated resume. Uploaded any optional recommendation letters they wish to include. Reviewed their application carefully for accuracy. Conclusion The USDA Spring 2027 Internship Program provides U.S. citizens interested in public service with an opportunity to work directly within the U.S. Department of Agriculture in Washington, D.C. Running from January 25 to April 30, 2027 , the program offers exposure to federal government operations, leadership, policymaking, agriculture, food systems, conservation, communications, rural development and other areas central to USDA s national mission. A major advantage of the current program is its broad educational eligibility: applicants do not have to be currently enrolled in college and do not need a university degree. USDA requires applicants to be U.S. citizens and at least 18 years old. At the same time, prospective applicants should understand the financial commitment involved. The internship is unpaid, fully in person in Washington, D.C., and provides neither intern housing nor relocation assistance . Candidates who can meet those requirements and want practical exposure to federal public service should prepare their materials early. Applications for the Spring 2027 cohort must be submitted by November 13, 2026 . For more global opportunities, click HERE . title: GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship 2026–2027: Global Opportunity for Education System Leaders to Transform Education at Scale
summary: The GIFTS – Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems is a new global fellowship designed for influential education system leaders who are working to reshape education systems and create better futures for children and young people. The fellowship brings together a carefully selected group of education system leaders from different countries for a year-long, cohort-based leadership and learning experience . Participants will have opportunities to engage with leading voices in education, collaborate with peers from around the world, receive mentoring and coaching, explore complex system-change challenges and participate in an in-person education-system immersion. The programme is designed around the idea that education systems must evolve in response to major economic, technological and climatic changes while ensuring that every child has the opportunity to learn, thrive and develop the purpose, agency and abilities needed to shape a better future. For education leaders working at a national or regional system level, the GIFTS Fellowship offers an opportunity to strengthen their leadership capabilities, expand their international networks, and develop locally rooted but globally informed approaches to education-system transformation. What Is the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship? GIFTS stands for the Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems . It is a new fellowship created to address a gap experienced by education-system leaders who are working to transform complex education systems but may have limited opportunities to connect with other leaders facing similar challenges. Education-system transformation can involve working across ministries, government institutions, schools, teachers, communities, civil society organisations and other stakeholders. Leaders responsible for this work must often navigate competing interests, political realities, changing technologies, economic pressures and evolving expectations about what education systems should deliver. The GIFTS Fellowship is intended to create a global community in which such leaders can learn from one another, exchange experiences and develop the capabilities required to lead system-wide transformation. The fellowship will bring together 20 influential education system insiders from diverse countries for a year-long experience combining virtual learning, peer engagement, mentoring, coaching and an in-person immersion. Why Was the GIFTS Fellowship Created? Education systems around the world are operating in an increasingly fast-changing environment. Economic developments, technological advances and climate-related changes are creating new challenges and opportunities for education. At the same time, education systems are expected to ensure that children and young people develop not only academic capabilities but also the purpose and agency required to navigate an uncertain future. The fellowship recognises that education-system leaders play a critical role in responding to these changes. These leaders are expected to: Chart new paths for their education systems. Adapt institutions and strategies to changing realities. Improve the performance of complex systems. Mobilise people at different levels of the education system. Inspire students, teachers and school leaders. Work with government and other partners. Address difficult system-level challenges. Develop strategies capable of producing sustainable change. Despite the importance and complexity of this work, education-system leaders may have relatively few opportunities to connect with peers, reflect on their experiences and share practical lessons about what it takes to transform education systems. The GIFTS Fellowship has been launched to help address this gap by creating a structured global learning environment for education-system leaders. What Will GIFTS Fellows Explore? The fellowship will encourage participants to investigate fundamental questions about education-system transformation. Among the questions highlighted by the programme are What outcomes should education systems achieve for all students today? How can the practices, structures and culture of an education system be aligned around its core purpose? What are the most effective strategies for improving the quality of learning in classrooms? What does improving classroom learning require from education-system leaders themselves? These questions place system leadership at the centre of the fellowship. Rather than looking only at individual schools or isolated education interventions, the programme focuses on the broader structures, practices, cultures and leadership approaches that determine how education systems operate. Who Is the GIFTS Fellowship Designed For? The GIFTS Fellowship is intended for influential and innovative education system leaders . The programme specifically identifies leaders working within: Ministries. Political offices. Civil society roles involving long-term partnerships with government. This means the fellowship is targeted primarily at people who have the ability to influence education systems at a significant level. It is not presented as a general scholarship or fellowship for students, recent graduates or people simply interested in education. Instead, the target participants are individuals already positioned within education systems or closely connected to government and capable of contributing to system-level transformation. The programme seeks leaders who can demonstrate both a track record of commitment and the potential to influence education beyond their immediate organisation or role. Qualities Expected of GIFTS Fellows According to the fellowship information, successful fellows will demonstrate several important characteristics. 1. Commitment to Improving Systems Around Children Fellows should have a lifelong commitment to improving the systems that shape children s lives and educational experiences. This means the programme is interested in leaders whose work goes beyond individual short-term interventions and is connected to improving the broader systems surrounding children. 2. Commitment to Holistic Student Development Applicants should align with the purpose of developing all students holistically, regardless of their background or economic circumstances. This reflects the fellowship s emphasis on creating education systems that provide opportunities for every student rather than benefiting only particular groups. 3. Collective Leadership Education-system transformation rarely happens through the work of one individual. The fellowship therefore seeks leaders with the capacity to develop collective leadership and work effectively with others. This can involve bringing together different stakeholders, building shared ownership and navigating the relationships necessary to move system-level initiatives forward. 4. Ability to Navigate Complex Politics Transforming education systems can involve complex political and institutional environments. The fellowship therefore looks for individuals capable of navigating political complexity while maintaining focus on system-level objectives. 5. Ability to Influence System-Level Change Applicants should have the ability to influence significant change at a national or regional scale . This is an important distinction because the fellowship is designed for system leaders whose influence extends beyond a single classroom, school or small community initiative. 6. Potential for Global Education Leadership The programme also seeks individuals who have the potential to become influential leaders within the wider global education ecosystem. This suggests that the fellowship is designed not only to strengthen participants current leadership but also to contribute to the development of a broader international community of education-system leaders. What Does the GIFTS Fellowship Offer? The fellowship provides a comprehensive learning and leadership experience lasting approximately one year. The programme will combine several components, allowing fellows to learn through formal sessions, peer interaction, coaching, mentoring and practical exploration. The major components include A curated international cohort. System Change Labs. Virtual masterclasses. Roundtables with senior education leaders. Peer-learning groups. Leadership sessions. Mentoring. Coaching. A four-day in-person immersion. The Better Future Forum. Continued participation in a global community of system leaders. Cohort-Based Learning Experience The GIFTS Fellowship will bring together 20 education system leaders from diverse countries . The cohort model is designed to create an environment in which participants can build trusting and enduring relationships with peers. This peer network is particularly important because education-system leaders often face similar challenges even when they work in very different national contexts. Through shared learning and reflection, fellows can exchange experiences and gain perspectives from leaders operating in other education systems. The programme aims to create relationships that extend beyond the formal fellowship period and contribute to a lasting global community. System Change Lab The System Change Lab is a practical component of the fellowship. Participants will explore and address a problem of practice during the fellowship. Rather than simply discussing system transformation at a theoretical level, fellows will have an opportunity to work on an issue connected to their own professional context. The lab will use: Action. Reflection. Peer feedback. Exploration of practical challenges. Generation of new insights. This approach is intended to help fellows connect leadership learning with real system-level challenges. Four-Day Education System Immersion Another major component is the Immersion Event . Fellows will participate in a four-day in-person immersive learning experience within an education system undergoing transformation. The immersion will give participants opportunities to engage with: Ministers. Schools. Practitioners. Fellow participants. Other education-system stakeholders. The programme identifies the four-day immersion as required . This practical exposure can enable fellows to observe system transformation in action and examine how leadership, policy, institutions and educational practice interact. Masterclasses and Roundtables Fellows will also participate in curated masterclasses and roundtable sessions involving senior global education leaders. These are described as closed-door sessions where participants can engage in honest conversations about the realities of system transformation. Topics can include: Difficult trade-offs. Failures. Breakthroughs. Leadership decisions. System-level challenges. Strategies for transformation. The focus on honest dialogue is intended to create a learning environment where leaders can discuss not only successful initiatives but also the difficulties and failures that accompany complex system change. Shared Inquiry and Peer Learning The fellowship places significant emphasis on learning with and from peers. Participants will form a curated cohort of education-system leaders and develop trusting relationships that support deeper learning. Peer interaction can help fellows compare experiences across different contexts, question assumptions and explore alternative approaches to leadership and system transformation. Triad Model Coaching GIFTS will use a three-part coaching and support model. The model brings together: Policy Mentors Policy mentors provide subject expertise and help participants think through policy-related questions and challenges. Leadership Coaches Leadership coaches support fellows as they navigate execution, uncertainty and difficult trade-offs associated with leadership. Peer Coaches Peer coaches contribute shared learning, accountability and feedback. Together, these three forms of support are intended to provide a more comprehensive development experience, combining technical or policy expertise with leadership guidance and peer support. The Better Future Forum Fellows will also have an opportunity to participate in the Global Institute s annual Better Future Forum . The forum is an in-person event that provides an opportunity to connect with leaders from the global education ecosystem. Participation in the Better Future Forum is listed as optional , unlike the four-day January immersion, which is specifically identified as required. Building a Lifelong Global Community The fellowship is designed to extend beyond the formal learning sessions. Participants will have opportunities to exchange practices across geographical boundaries and may have the option of visiting other fellows. The programme aims to build a lifelong global community of education-system leaders who can continue learning from one another and sharing practices after the formal fellowship concludes. This international network is potentially one of the most valuable aspects of the programme for leaders working on complex education-system challenges. GIFTS Fellowship 2026–2027 Timeline The fellowship follows a year-long schedule beginning in 2026 and continuing through September 2027. Application Stage June 2026: Applications open. 11 September 2026: Applications close. October 2026: Selection announced. Fellowship Journey The fellowship programme then continues through a combination of virtual and in-person activities: October 2026 Virtual launch event. November–December 2026 Virtual lab. Masterclasses. Peer sessions. Leadership sessions. January 2027 Four-day in-person immersion event. Attendance is required. February–April 2027 Virtual lab. Masterclasses. Peer sessions. Leadership sessions. May 2027 Better Future Forum. Three-day in-person event. Participation is optional. June–August 2027 Virtual lab. Masterclasses. Peer sessions. Leadership sessions. September 2027 Virtual graduation. How to Apply for the GIFTS Fellowship Individuals interested in the GIFTS Fellowship can submit an application through the fellowship s application portal. The programme asks applicants to refer to the application guidance contained in the fellowship blueprint document when preparing their applications. Application deadline: 11 September 2026. Prospective applicants should review the application guidance carefully and ensure that their experience and leadership profile clearly demonstrate the qualities sought by the fellowship. APPLY HERE Nominations Are Also Welcome The GIFTS Fellowship does not rely solely on self-nomination. The organisers also welcome nominations of exceptional system leaders who are working at the forefront of education-system transformation and shaping a better future for children and young people. However, a nomination is not an application and does not guarantee selection . If a nominee appears to meet the fellowship s eligibility criteria, they may subsequently be invited to submit a full application. Submit a GIFTS Fellowship Nomination This nomination route creates an opportunity for organisations, colleagues and other stakeholders to identify education leaders whose work deserves consideration. Global Eligibility and Geographic Reach The GIFTS Fellowship is explicitly described as a global fellowship . The programme aims to bring together education-system leaders from countries around the world and states that the cohort will include leaders from diverse countries. The supplied information does not provide a specific list of eligible countries or continents. It also does not identify any race or ethnicity restrictions. Therefore, the opportunity should be understood as internationally oriented, while applicants should consult the official application guidance to determine whether any additional eligibility conditions apply. What Kind of Leader Is Best Suited to GIFTS? The GIFTS Fellowship is particularly suited to an education professional who is already working on system-level change rather than someone who is simply beginning a career in education. A potentially strong candidate would be someone whose work involves influencing education policy, institutions, government systems, regional or national education strategies, or long-term government partnerships. The fellowship may be particularly relevant to leaders who are: Working within education ministries. Working within political offices connected to education. Leading civil society initiatives in long-term partnership with government. Influencing education policy or system reform. Working on national or regional education transformation. Building collective leadership across complex education systems. Developing innovative approaches to improving outcomes for children. Seeking to strengthen their international education leadership network. The programme s stated eligibility profile places considerable emphasis on influence, innovation, system-level change and leadership potential . Programme Commitments and Participation The fellowship involves a mixture of virtual and in-person activities spread across approximately one year. Participants should therefore be prepared to engage consistently with the fellowship journey. The programme includes recurring virtual labs, masterclasses, peer and leadership sessions, as well as the required four-day in-person immersion in January 2027. The Better Future Forum in May 2027 is identified as optional. The supplied source also points applicants toward a separate programme information document containing additional details concerning the curriculum, faculty and fellowship commitments. View the GIFTS Programme Information, Curriculum and Fellowship Commitments Why the GIFTS Fellowship Could Be Valuable for Education Leaders Education-system leaders often work in environments where change is difficult because systems involve many interconnected institutions and stakeholders. A change in one part of an education system can have consequences elsewhere. Leaders may therefore need to balance policy objectives, institutional realities, stakeholder interests, political considerations and the needs of students. The GIFTS Fellowship is structured around precisely these kinds of challenges. Its combination of peer learning, system-change work, mentoring, leadership coaching and exposure to other education systems can provide participants with multiple perspectives on how large-scale transformation can be approached. The international cohort also creates an opportunity to compare approaches across countries and learn how different leaders respond to similar challenges in different contexts. Important Information for Prospective Applicants Before applying or accepting a nomination, prospective fellows should carefully review the official programme guidance. In particular, applicants should pay attention to: The eligibility profile: The programme is seeking influential and innovative education-system leaders rather than applicants at any career stage. Leadership experience: Applicants should be able to demonstrate their capacity to influence system-level change at national or regional scale. Government connection: The programme specifically identifies people working within ministries, political offices or civil society roles involving long-term government partnerships. International orientation: The fellowship brings together leaders from diverse countries and is designed to develop a global community. Time commitment: The programme runs for approximately one year and involves virtual and in-person activities. Required immersion: The four-day January 2027 in-person immersion is listed as required. Optional forum: The three-day Better Future Forum in May 2027 is listed as optional. Application deadline: Applications close on 11 September 2026. Nominations: A nomination does not constitute an application and does not guarantee selection. Visit HERE for more information about the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship 2026–2027. Frequently Asked Questions About the GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship What does GIFTS stand for? GIFTS stands for Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems . Who is the fellowship for? It is designed for influential and innovative education-system leaders working within ministries, political offices or civil society roles that involve long-term partnerships with government. How many fellows will be selected? The fellowship will bring together 20 influential education system insiders from diverse countries. How long does the fellowship last? The GIFTS Fellowship is structured as a year-long cohort-based experience , beginning with the virtual launch in October 2026 and concluding with virtual graduation in September 2027. When is the application deadline? Applications close on 11 September 2026 . Is the fellowship open internationally? The programme is explicitly described as a global fellowship and intends to bring together leaders from diverse countries around the world. The supplied source does not provide a specific list of eligible countries. Are nominations accepted? Yes. The organisers welcome nominations of exceptional education-system leaders. However, a nomination does not guarantee selection and is not itself an application. A nominee who appears to meet the eligibility criteria may be invited to submit a full application. Is the in-person immersion mandatory? Yes. The January 2027 immersion is described as a four-day in-person event and required . Is the Better Future Forum mandatory? The source identifies the May 2027 Better Future Forum as a three-day in-person event that is optional . What kind of coaching is offered? The fellowship uses a triad model combining policy mentors for subject expertise, leadership coaches for navigating execution and uncertainty, and peer coaches for shared learning, accountability and feedback. What is the System Change Lab? It is a fellowship component through which participants explore and address a problem of practice, generating insights through action, reflection and peer feedback. Conclusion The GIFTS Global Institute Fellowship for Transforming Systems is a global leadership opportunity for education-system leaders who are working to create meaningful and sustainable change at a national or regional scale. The fellowship goes beyond conventional professional development by bringing together a select cohort of 20 influential education leaders for a year-long experience combining peer learning, system-change work, global masterclasses, mentoring, leadership coaching and practical immersion. Its focus is particularly relevant to leaders who work within ministries, political offices or civil society organisations engaged in long-term partnerships with government. The programme seeks people who demonstrate a sustained commitment to improving systems around children, can develop collective leadership, can navigate complex political environments and have the ability to influence significant education-system change. For successful fellows, the experience is designed to strengthen their leadership capabilities, broaden their global perspective, develop new insights into system transformation and connect them with a lifelong international community of education-system leaders.
