title: DA Young Leaders Programme 2027: Applications Open for Young South Africans Interested in Political and Public Service Leadership
summary: Applications are now open for the 2027 Democratic Alliance (DA) Young Leaders Programme (YLP) , a one-year political leadership learning and development programme designed for young South Africans who are passionate about leadership, public service, politics and creating positive change in their communities. The programme provides an opportunity for motivated young people to strengthen their political knowledge, critical-thinking abilities, communication skills and personal leadership capabilities while gaining practical experience through a dedicated leadership project. For young South Africans considering a future in politics, government, public service or community leadership, the DA Young Leaders Programme offers structured leadership development designed to help participants understand their leadership potential, identify areas for personal growth, and develop the skills required to become effective changemakers. About the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027 The DA Young Leaders Programme is described as a political leadership learning and development programme for South Africans aged between 18 and 35 who align themselves with the Democratic Alliance s values of Freedom, Fairness, Opportunity and Diversity . The programme is aimed at highly motivated individuals who are interested in pursuing a career in politics or the public service and who want to contribute to building what the DA describes as One Nation with One Future. Rather than focusing only on theoretical leadership concepts, the programme combines political learning, personal development, communication development and practical leadership experience. Participants are expected to develop a stronger understanding of politics while also gaining greater insight into their own leadership style, strengths and development needs. Over the course of one year, Young Leaders participate in activities intended to broaden their political knowledge and critical-thinking capabilities. They also develop communication skills and take part in dedicated sessions focused on leadership and personal development. A central component of the programme is the requirement for each participant to conceptualise and undertake a leadership project . This gives participants an opportunity to apply what they learn in a practical setting while addressing an issue within their community. Who Should Apply for the DA Young Leaders Programme? The programme is designed for young people who are not only interested in leadership but are already demonstrating a commitment to making a positive difference in their communities. According to the programme information, successful applicants are expected to demonstrate qualities such as Integrity and a strong commitment to serving others. Leadership potential and motivation to create meaningful change. A desire to continue developing their personal and professional potential. An interest in politics, public service or government as a potential career path. A passion for contributing to a better future for South Africa. The ability to align their personal values with the Democratic Alliance s liberal values and principles. An interest in strengthening their critical-thinking, communication, writing, public-speaking, and leadership skills. The programme therefore goes beyond identifying young people who simply have an interest in politics. It seeks individuals who demonstrate leadership potential, community commitment and a willingness to take responsibility for creating meaningful change. What Participants Can Gain from the Young Leaders Programme The DA Young Leaders Programme provides a combination of political education, leadership development, personal development and practical experience. 1. Political Knowledge and Understanding Participants have the opportunity to broaden their understanding of politics and develop greater political knowledge. This can help them better understand the issues affecting South Africa and the role that effective leadership can play in addressing national and community challenges. The political learning component is particularly relevant for young people considering future careers in political leadership, government or public service. 2. Critical-Thinking Skills Critical thinking is another important area of development within the programme. Participants are challenged to think critically and develop the ability to engage with issues in a thoughtful and informed manner. These skills can be valuable for people interested in policy, public leadership, government and community development. 3. Communication Development Communication is a major component of effective leadership, and the programme provides participants with opportunities to strengthen their communication abilities. Participants are expected to develop their: Writing skills Public-speaking abilities General communication skills Ability to express ideas effectively Capacity to engage with political and community issues These skills can be particularly valuable for aspiring public representatives and future leaders. 4. Personal Leadership Development The programme also places considerable emphasis on personal development. Participants are given opportunities to understand themselves better, including their individual leadership styles and areas where they need further development. Dedicated leadership and personal-development sessions are intended to support this process. This emphasis means that the programme is not solely focused on external leadership responsibilities. It also encourages participants to develop self-awareness and understand how their individual characteristics can influence the way they lead. 5. Practical Leadership Experience One of the distinguishing elements of the programme is the leadership project that every participant is required to undertake. Through this project, participants are able to move beyond classroom or theoretical learning and apply their leadership skills to a real-world challenge. The programme states that these projects provide experience in areas such as: Planning Collaboration Community engagement Leadership Problem-solving Public leadership This practical experience can help participants build confidence and develop a stronger understanding of what effective leadership looks like in real communities. Leadership in Action: The Programme s Community Projects The leadership project component is intended to create meaningful impact within participants communities. According to the programme information, previous projects have addressed a range of social and community challenges. Examples provided by the programme include initiatives focused on gender-based violence awareness, school support, youth employment, housing and education. Examples include: Anti-Gender-Based Violence Awareness Some Young Leaders have developed campaigns focused on raising awareness about gender-based violence. These initiatives have included empowering young women and organising public gatherings against gender-based violence. Such projects demonstrate how leadership development can be connected to advocacy and community mobilisation. School Support Initiatives Other projects have focused on supporting disadvantaged schoolchildren. The examples include initiatives that provided children with essential items such as proper shoes, with the broader aim of supporting their confidence and sense of pride. Female Youth Employment Projects Some participants have worked on projects designed to address youth employment challenges among disadvantaged girls. These initiatives have sought to help bridge the gap between secondary education and full-time employment, demonstrating how Young Leaders can use community projects to address barriers facing young people. Housing and Education Projects Other leadership projects have addressed housing and community resilience. The programme highlights projects involving the construction of houses in vulnerable areas of the Western Cape, alongside efforts to educate local communities about the use of sandbag systems for flood protection. These examples illustrate the practical dimension of the Young Leaders Programme: participants are expected to use their leadership skills to engage with genuine challenges and develop initiatives that can produce tangible community benefits. The DA Young Leaders Programme s Long-Term Impact The Young Leaders Programme has already developed a substantial alumni network. According to the programme s information, more than 330 graduates have completed the programme since its launch. These alumni are described as making an impact across South Africa in public office, within the Democratic Alliance and through community initiatives. The programme reports the following impact figures: 330+ graduates have completed the Young Leaders Programme. 84 alumni are currently serving in public office, including as Members of Parliament, Members of Provincial Legislatures, councillors and other elected representatives. 7 members of the Democratic Alliance s leadership are alumni of the Young Leaders Programme. Alumni continue to contribute through community initiatives, public service and policy development across South Africa. These figures demonstrate the programme s stated role in developing a pipeline of young people who can go on to participate in political leadership, public service and community development. The Programme s Vision for South Africa The Young Leaders Programme is connected to the DA s broader vision for South Africa. The programme s stated vision is for a South Africa in which individuals have the opportunity to live lives that they value. It describes a country characterised by a dynamic and innovative society, an inclusive and growing economy, and a capable government that protects the Constitution and promotes equal opportunity. The vision emphasises equal opportunity regardless of where people are born, how they look or other arbitrary characteristics. The programme argues that achieving such a vision requires excellent leaders who are prepared to step forward and lead. Consequently, the Young Leaders Programme is positioned as part of the effort to prepare young South Africans for future leadership responsibilities. Eligibility for the DA Young Leaders Programme 2027 The source identifies the programme as being open to South Africans between the ages of 18 and 35 who align with the DA s stated values of Freedom, Fairness, Opportunity and Diversity. Are already making a positive impact in their communities. Demonstrate integrity and a commitment to serving others. Want to strengthen their political knowledge and critical-thinking skills. Want to improve their writing, public-speaking, and communication abilities. Are willing to undertake a leadership project. Can align their personal values with the DA s stated liberal values and principles. The source also lists a series of frequently asked questions concerning matters such as time commitment, age requirements, participation while working or studying full-time, retreats, transportation, leadership projects, costs, selection numbers, tertiary qualifications, previous applications and prior participation in other DA leadership programmes. However, the supplied source does not provide the answers to those questions, so applicants should not assume requirements or conditions that are not expressly stated.
